classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: radial_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the collisionless free-streaming bound on
ion momentum flux along the major-radius direction, limiting flux magnitude
without reversing its direction.
items.documentation:
The radial ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient scales the collisionless
free-streaming bound on gradient-driven transport of ion
[momentum](name:momentum) along the major-radius direction. It caps the flux
magnitude without reversing its direction. Here radial denotes increasing
major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$\phi$ is toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The limiting flux magnitude is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{i,R}^{\max} = \alpha_{i,R}\,\Pi_{i,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Pi_{i,R}^{\max}$ is the upper bound on the magnitude of the limited
momentum flux, $\alpha_{i,R}$ is this coefficient, and
$\Pi_{i,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming reference
magnitude. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion population, and $R$
identifies the major-radius transport direction. This relation does not
prescribe a particular interpolation between gradient-driven transport and
the limiting bound.

This is the major-radius component of the [ion momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), not a sum over
directional coefficients. It applies to ion momentum transport rather than
neutral momentum transport and is not restricted to one specified ion charge
state. The coefficient is neither a momentum diffusivity nor a spatial
coordinate.

The major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux
surface. The [poloidal ion momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) is a
distinct directional member of the same family.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_coil_conductor_element
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of a coil-conductor element reference point, equal
to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of coil conductor element

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the reference point's transverse coordinates in a
right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ frame whose $z$ axis coincides with the
toroidal symmetry axis; $z$ denotes vertical height.

This quantity locates the selected reference point of an individual
coil-conductor element, without averaging over the conductor or coil. It is
not an arc radius or a displacement measured from the conductor centerline.

items.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the φ component, in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the density-weighted mean bulk
flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to the
confined core.
items.documentation:
Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the $\phi$ component, in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of the density-weighted mean
bulk flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to
the confined core. As an intensive species-level quantity, it is the
density-weighted mean over all argon charge states, not a
charge-state-summed velocity.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by the density-weighted mean at the
pedestal top:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}^{\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes argon ionization state,
$n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the local number density of that
charge state, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is its toroidal
velocity component at the pedestal top.

It is inferred primarily from Doppler spectroscopy of argon emission, often
charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy when suitable neutral-beam
excitation is available. The observed line shift and viewing geometry
determine the velocity projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; estimating the
all-charge-state mean may require emissivity modeling, ionization-balance
information, or collisional equilibration assumptions.

Because pedestal argon rotation is sensitive to external torque, radial
electric-field shear, neoclassical friction, turbulence-driven momentum
transport, and charge-state distribution, no device-independent numerical
range is implied. This value is commonly interpreted with same-species
values at other loci, including [toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), [toroidal argon
velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
[toroidal argon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and toroidal
flux-surface-averaged argon velocity at the plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted mean argon flow points
in the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

items.name: hot_neutral_velocity
items.description:
Hot neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk flow of an
energetic neutral atom population, identified from the Doppler centroid
shift of its broad emission component.
items.documentation:
Hot neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk drift vector
of a hot neutral particle population. It represents convective neutral
motion after averaging over particle velocities and over the contributing
hot-neutral internal-state or energy subpopulations.

At position $\mathbf r$, the projected component is the first velocity
moment of the selected hot neutral distribution projected along the line of
sight:

$$
u_{\mathrm{hot},\mathrm{los}}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\ell}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hot}}}\int \mathbf v\,f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hot}}}\int f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $\mathbf r$ is position, $\hat{\ell}$ is the line-of-sight direction
from the first point to the second point, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity,
$f_{n,a}$ is the phase-space density of neutral subpopulation $a$, and
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hot}}$ is the included set of hot neutral
subpopulations.

The scope is restricted to energetic neutrals in the selected hot
population; colder neutral components are excluded unless they are part of
that selected population. The scalar is a directional projection of [neutral
velocity](name:neutral_velocity), not the magnitude of the neutral flow
vector, a particle flux, a momentum density, or a thermal spread.

It is the hot-population counterpart of [cold neutral
velocity](name:cold_neutral_velocity). It is distinct from [hot neutral
temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature_at_plasma_boundary), which
characterizes random velocity spread rather than the centroid or
first-moment drift of the hot neutral population.

Sign convention: Positive when the hot-neutral bulk drift projects from the
first point to the second point along the line of sight.

items.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_camera
items.description:
Signed direction cosine giving a camera’s pointing direction along the y
axis of the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The camera direction-vector component along the y axis is the signed
direction cosine of its pointing direction in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis. It specifies the projection of the camera
viewing direction onto the Cartesian y axis.

The component is defined by

$$
d_y = \hat{\mathbf{d}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{d}}$ is the camera pointing-direction unit vector and
$\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the positive y-axis unit vector. Its value forms part
of the normalized direction vector together with the [x-axis camera
direction component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [z-axis
camera direction component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera),
satisfying $d_x^2+d_y^2+d_z^2=1$.

This quantity describes camera pointing direction, not image-up orientation;
that distinct orientation is represented by the [camera y image-up
unit-vector component](name:y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera).

items.name: power_density_due_to_fusion
items.description:
Local volumetric rate of energy release from all included nuclear-fusion
reaction channels, including energy carried by charged particles and
neutrons.
items.documentation:
Fusion power density is the local energy-release rate generated by
nuclear-fusion reactions per unit volume. It may represent a specific
reaction channel or the channel-summed quantity, with unqualified fusion
power density understood as the sum over included channels.

The defining reaction-rate sum is

$$
P_{\mathrm{fus}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} \frac{n_{a,r}(\mathbf{x})\,n_{b,r}(\mathbf{x})}{1+\delta_{a_rb_r}}\,\langle\sigma v\rangle_r\,E_r
$$

where $r$ indexes fusion channels, $n_{a,r}$ and $n_{b,r}$ are reactant
number densities in m$^{-3}$, $\langle\sigma v\rangle_r$ is the
reaction-rate coefficient in m$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$, $E_r$ is the energy released
per reaction in joules, and $\delta_{a_rb_r}$ is one for identical reactants
and zero otherwise. The deuterium–deuterium and deuterium–tritium instances
are represented by [deuterium-deuterium fusion power
density](name:deuterium_deuterium_power_density_due_to_fusion) and
[deuterium-tritium fusion power
density](name:deuterium_tritium_power_density_due_to_fusion). This
energy-release quantity includes neutron and charged-particle product energy
and is distinct from fusion neutron emissivity.

items.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous rate of electron-equivalent particles supplied by active
injection, obtained by nuclear-charge weighting each injected atomic
species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection
systems, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis when multiple injected
species are combined. It represents the electron inventory that the supplied
material can contribute after ionization.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=\sum_s Z_s\dot{N}_s(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $\dot{N}_s$ are source rates, $s$ indexes
the injected atomic species, and $Z_s$ is the dimensionless nuclear charge
number. For molecular feeds, each constituent atom is included with its
nuclear-charge weighting. This is the charge-weighted instance of the
[source rate due to injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection); for
unit-charge deuterium, it equals the [deuterium source rate due to
injection](name:deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection).

This is an injected inventory rate, not a local volumetric particle source
or a net plasma production-minus-loss rate such as the [total electron
source rate](name:total_electron_source_rate).

Sign convention: Positive when active injection increases the supplied
equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field
items.description:
Complex first-order radial component of the magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum outside the plasma, forming part of
a single-toroidal-mode linear MHD perturbation.
items.documentation:
The radial component of the perturbed vacuum magnetic field is the
projection of the complex first-order magnetic-field eigenfunction onto the
cylindrical radial direction in the current-free exterior region. It is one
component of the full [perturbed vacuum magnetic
field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field), which satisfies source-free
Maxwell conditions in the vacuum.

The component is defined by

$$
\delta B_R = \delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the perturbed vacuum magnetic-field
vector, $\hat{R}$ is the radial unit vector, and $\delta B_R$ is its radial
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The radial
direction means increasing major radius $R$, not the normal to a magnetic
flux surface.

The complex value retains the eigenfunction amplitude and phase; its
in-phase and quadrature coefficients are represented by the [real radial
component](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part) and
[imaginary radial
component](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part). In
the current-free vacuum, the perturbation obeys
$\nabla\times\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}=0$ and
$\nabla\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}=0$.

Sign convention: Positive when the radial component is directed along
increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame.

items.name: parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
items.description:
Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned kinetic
pressure moment of suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It
is defined locally; its flux-surface-averaged form is the average of that
moment over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned component of
the kinetic stress carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped
orbits. It is distinct from the scalar trace pressure of the same
population.

The local parallel pressure is the second velocity moment of the trapped
fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast,tr}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the parallel trapped fast-particle
pressure, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $c$
labels charge state where applicable, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the
velocity-space number-density distribution restricted to trapped
suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$. The integral is
over velocity space, with $d^3v$ its volume element. The field-aligned
velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude.

The population comprises trapped nonthermal particles; thermal particles and
co-passing and counter-passing particles are excluded. Contributions are
added over fast-particle species and charge states, rather than
density-weighted. The local moment retains variation within a magnetic flux
surface; its flux-surface average is the average of the local moment over
that surface. The second moment is not centered on the population mean
velocity, so directed field-aligned motion contributes to the stress.

This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [parallel fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure). Together with
[perpendicular trapped fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), it determines
the [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure),
which is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace:
$p_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast,tr}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast,tr}})/3$.
Here $p_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the scalar trace pressure of the same trapped
population, and $p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is its perpendicular stress per
transverse degree of freedom.

items.name: energy_flux_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Local rate of energy deposition per unit divertor-target area, combining all
incident particle and radiative energy-carrying channels.
items.documentation:
Energy flux at a divertor target is the local surface density of power
deposited by incident plasma and radiative energy carriers on the
target-facing surface. It describes the energy load at each surface location
rather than power integrated over a target or divertor assembly.

The local energy flux is defined by

$$
q_E(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{\mathrm{d}P_E}{\mathrm{d}A}
$$

where $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ is the deposited energy flux at surface position
$\mathbf{x}$, $P_E$ is the cumulative deposited power from all included
incident energy carriers, and $A$ is target-surface area.

The quantity applies to one divertor target surface and combines the
contributions of incident particle and radiative energy channels. It does
not resolve separate electron, ion, conductive, convective,
neutral-particle, or radiative contributions, and it is not a
target-integrated power.

This quantity is the energy-deposition component represented by [flux at a
divertor target](name:flux_at_divertor_target); the latter provides the
carrier-independent target-surface load. The corresponding surface maximum,
[maximum of energy flux at a divertor
target](name:energy_flux_maximum_at_divertor_target), is obtained by
selecting the largest value of $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ over the target surface.

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
items.description:
Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of
suprathermal ions in a specified ionization state, formed from velocity
fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is represented by the
parallel and perpendicular pressure components relative to the local
magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of
suprathermal ions for a specified ion species and ionization state, formed
from velocity fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is
represented by the pair of pressure components parallel and perpendicular to
the local magnetic-field direction; this pair parameterizes a gyrotropic
pressure tensor and is not a spatial vector.

The component pair is defined from the fast-ion distribution function by the
velocity-fluctuation moments:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}} \\
p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}
\end{pmatrix}
=
m_s \int f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})
\begin{pmatrix}
[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]^2 \\
\frac{1}{2}\left|(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})-[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]\mathbf{b}\right|^2
\end{pmatrix}
\, d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ and
$p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ are the pressure components for species $s$
in ionization state $q$, $m_s$ is the ion mass for species $s$,
$f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal part of the distribution
function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the mean flow velocity of the same
population, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field,
and the integral is over velocity space.

The scope is gyrotropic pressure: the two transverse directions
perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$ are averaged, so the perpendicular component
is one half of the transverse fluctuation moment. A fully non-gyrotropic
pressure tensor with unequal transverse components or off-diagonal terms is
outside this standard name. Because pressure is an extensive per-volume
velocity moment, aggregate [parallel fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure) are obtained by summing the
corresponding components over all fast-ion species and ionization states.

items.name: hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Local number density of hydrogen ions at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge pedestal, summed over all hydrogen ion charge states and
excluding neutral hydrogen.
items.documentation:
Hydrogen ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local count of hydrogen ions per unit volume at the pedestal's core-side
shoulder. It is specific to hydrogen ions rather than the total ion
population.

The charge-state-summed hydrogen ion density is defined by:

$$
n_{\mathrm H} = \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{\mathrm H}^{(Z+)}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm H}$ is the local hydrogen-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm
H}^{(Z+)}$ is the local number density of hydrogen ions with charge state
$Z+$, and $Z$ is the positive integer charge-state index.

This quantity applies locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined
by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). The
aggregation is a sum over all hydrogen ion charge states; neutral hydrogen
and ions of other elements are excluded.

It differs from [flux-surface-averaged hydrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which is averaged over a flux surface and evaluated at the plasma boundary,
and from [hydrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which has a different
spatial locus.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity coefficient relating convective transport of toroidal
momentum across an oriented surface to the toroidal momentum density of one
resolved neutral internal state.
items.documentation:
This effective convection velocity multiplies the toroidal
[momentum](name:momentum) density of one neutral internal state to give its
convective flux through an oriented surface. The toroidal label identifies
the transported momentum component, not the direction of transport. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing toroidal angle.

For a surface with chosen unit normal $\hat{\mathbf n}$, the defining
convective closure is:

$$
\Pi_{s,\phi n}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}} M_{s,\phi}
$$

where $s$ identifies one internal state of one neutral species, $\Pi_{s,\phi
n}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its convective toroidal-momentum flux through the
oriented surface, $V_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection
coefficient, and $M_{s,\phi}$ is its toroidal momentum density. The momentum
density is $M_{s,\phi}=m_s n_s u_{s,\phi}$, where $m_s$ is the neutral
particle mass, $n_s$ is the state-resolved number density, and $u_{s,\phi}$
is the projection of the state's mean translational velocity onto
$\hat{\phi}$.

The quantity is resolved by neutral internal state, without summation over
states or species. Its [neutral-species
counterpart](name:toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity)
applies to momentum transport aggregated over internal states; state
momentum fluxes, rather than velocity coefficients, are additive.

This is a transport coefficient, not the toroidal projection of the [bulk
neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity),
and it need not equal that projection. It excludes gradient-driven diffusive
transport, represented by [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity),
and does not represent a momentum source.

Sign convention: Positive when effective convection is directed along the
chosen surface normal, so that convective toroidal-momentum flux and
toroidal momentum density have the same sign; positive toroidal momentum
points toward increasing $\phi$.

items.name: total_neutral_pressure
items.description:
Total pressure of a neutral species combines its thermal and nonthermal
pressure contributions, summed over charge states when multiple states are
represented. It applies to neutral populations in the core and edge plasma,
including the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
Total pressure of a neutral species combines the pressure contributions from
its thermal and nonthermal neutral populations. It denotes their total
pressure rather than either contribution alone.

The total pressure is the additive combination of the thermal and nonthermal
contributions:

$$
p_0 = p_{0,\mathrm{th}} + p_{0,\mathrm{nt}}
$$

where $p_0$ is the total pressure of the neutral species,
$p_{0,\mathrm{th}}$ is its [thermal neutral
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure), and $p_{0,\mathrm{nt}}$ is its
nonthermal pressure contribution, represented by [fast neutral
pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure). The subscript $0$ identifies neutral
particles; $\mathrm{th}$ and $\mathrm{nt}$ identify the thermal and
nonthermal contributions.

This species-level quantity applies to neutral populations in the core and
edge plasma, including the scrape-off layer. When multiple charge states are
represented, their pressure contributions are summed over all represented
charge states, not averaged. It includes both thermal and nonthermal
contributions, unlike the thermal-only pressure, and is not restricted to a
single internal state; the [total neutral internal-state
pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) resolves pressure by
internal state.

items.name: ion_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective vector velocity at which aggregate ion momentum is advectively
transported in plasma fluid models, serving as a closure coefficient
distinct from the actual bulk ion flow velocity.
items.documentation:
The ion momentum convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient in
the non-diffusive, advective transport of aggregate ion momentum. It is a
transport-closure quantity and is distinct from the material bulk ion
velocity, as distinguished from the broader momentum convection velocity
framework.

A transport-closure decomposition of ion momentum flux is written as

$$
\mathbf{F}_{p,i} = -D_{p,i}\nabla\mathbf{p}_i + \mathbf{V}_{c,i} \otimes \mathbf{p}_i
$$

where $\mathbf{F}_{p,i}$ is the ion momentum-flux tensor, $D_{p,i}$ is the
ion momentum diffusivity, $\mathbf{p}_i$ is ion momentum density, and
$\mathbf{V}_{c,i}$ is this convection velocity. The dyadic term represents
non-diffusive momentum transport.

The unqualified ion quantity aggregates the ion momentum contribution over
all charge states. A species- or charge-state-resolved form, such as [ion
charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), supplies the
corresponding resolved convention; unlike [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), this coefficient is not the
material flow velocity.

items.name: width_of_iron_core_segment
items.description:
Full non-negative radial extent of an iron core segment’s rectangular
cross-section, measured along major radius in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The iron core segment width is the complete radial span between the inner
and outer faces of its rectangular cross-section. It is a geometric extent,
not the radial position of the segment or the curvature radius of an arc
boundary.

The width is defined by

$$
w_{\rm iron} = R_{\rm outer} - R_{\rm inner}
$$

where $R_{\rm outer}$ and $R_{\rm inner}$ are the major-radius coordinates
in meters of the outer and inner radial faces, respectively, and $w_{\rm
iron}$ is the resulting full extent. The width complements the [height of
the iron core segment](name:height_of_iron_core_segment), while the [outer
radius of the iron core segment](name:outer_radius_of_iron_core_segment)
identifies a boundary position rather than a cross-sectional span.

items.name: total_electron_source_rate
items.description:
Total electron source rate is the net production or removal rate of free
electrons, summed over all contributing processes and integrated over the
entire plasma volume.
items.documentation:
Total electron source rate is the net rate at which free electrons are
produced or removed throughout the plasma volume. It is the global
particle-source contribution to electron-number balance.

The total rate is defined by

$$
S_e^{\mathrm{tot}} = \int_{\mathcal V_p} S_e^{\mathrm{vol}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $S_e^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total electron source rate, $\mathcal V_p$
is the entire plasma volume, $S_e^{\mathrm{vol}}$ is the [electron
volumetric source rate](name:electron_volumetric_source_rate) summed over
all contributing production and removal processes, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes
spatial position, and $dV$ is a physical volume element.

This quantity counts free electrons rather than electrons bound in atoms or
molecules. Positive values indicate net production and negative values
indicate net removal. It is a volume-integrated source, not a local
volumetric rate, a flux-surface average, or a particle transport flux
through the plasma boundary.

The [electron particle source rate inside a magnetic flux
surface](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_electron_particle_source_rate)
uses the same integral restricted to the enclosed volume; it equals this
total when that volume contains the entire plasma. Unlike [electron
deposited power](name:electron_deposited_power), this quantity describes
particle production or removal rather than energy transfer.

items.name: fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Fast-ion collisional torque density is the local vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer to fast ions per unit plasma volume caused by
Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
items.documentation:
Fast-ion collisional torque density is the local vector source of angular
momentum delivered to the fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It is
the fast-ion component of the broader [ion torque density due to
collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [thermal-ion
torque density due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) describes the
corresponding thermal-ion contribution.

The local defining relation is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_f}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{f,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-ion collisional
torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_f$ is fast-ion angular-momentum
density, and $t$ is time; the subscript $\mathrm{coll}$ selects the
Coulomb-collisional contribution. Orbit-resolved and component-resolved
forms are specific instances of this vector quantity, and it is distinct
from collisional energy-transfer density.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved vector component points along its
positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

items.name: parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density
items.description:
Parallel normalized particle perturbed current density is the normalized
parallel-current-density moment of the perturbed particle distribution for
one kinetic species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, projected along the
equilibrium magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Parallel normalized particle perturbed current density is the normalized
parallel-current-density moment of the perturbed particle distribution for
one kinetic species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. It represents the
species contribution to the perturbed current projected along the
equilibrium magnetic field in the particle frame.

The normalized moment is defined by the particle-frame parallel
current-density moment divided by its reference normalization:

$$
\hat{j}^{\,p}_{\parallel s} = \frac{\int q_s v_\parallel \delta f^{\,p}_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{j_\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\hat{j}^{\,p}_{\parallel s}$ is the parallel normalized particle
perturbed current density for species $s$, $q_s$ is the charge of that
species, $v_\parallel$ is the particle velocity component along the
equilibrium magnetic field, $\delta f^{\,p}_s$ is the perturbed particle
distribution function, $d^3v$ denotes integration over particle velocity
space, and $j_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference current-density scale for the
normalized moment.

The scope is a species-resolved linear perturbation moment at the selected
eigenmode and wavevector; the aggregation convention is per kinetic species,
with no summation over species. The quantity excludes equilibrium current
density and unperturbed distribution-function moments.

It is the particle-frame counterpart of parallel normalized perturbed
current density, which uses the gyrocenter perturbed distribution rather
than the particle distribution. The particle-frame moment can differ through
the gyrocenter-to-particle transformation, including
polarization-drift-related contributions when they are part of that
transformation. The corresponding particle-frame higher parallel-velocity
moment is parallel normalized particle perturbed heat flux.

Sign convention: Positive when the particle-frame perturbed current carried
by the species is directed along the equilibrium magnetic field.

items.name: neutral_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Vector diffusion coefficient for bulk neutral-particle momentum, governing
anisotropic diffusive redistribution driven by neutral-neutral viscosity and
charge-exchange collisions in edge and divertor plasma.
items.documentation:
Neutral momentum diffusivity is the direction-dependent transport
coefficient that relates the diffusive neutral-fluid momentum flux in each
spatial direction to the local gradient of neutral momentum density, forming
the neutral-particle analog of plasma_momentum_diffusivity. As a vector
quantity it encompasses distinct directional components — including
parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity,
poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity,
[toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity),
and
[vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity)
— reflecting the anisotropy imposed by the magnetic geometry and the varying
collisional regimes of edge and divertor regions.

The component $\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom}}$ along a direction $\hat{e}$ enters the
neutral fluid momentum balance through the diffusive flux:

$$
\Gamma_{n,\mathrm{mom}} = -\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom}} \, \nabla_{\hat{e}}(m_n n_n u_n)
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number
density, and $u_n$ is the neutral fluid velocity component along $\hat{e}$.

The dominant physical mechanisms contributing to neutral momentum
diffusivity are neutral-neutral viscous collisions and charge-exchange
interactions with background ions; the latter can transfer substantial
momentum between the neutral and ion populations and are especially
significant in dense regions where charge-exchange mean-free paths are
short. This coefficient is computed within fluid-neutral transport models
that solve the neutral momentum equation self-consistently alongside the
plasma fluid equations.

items.name: perturbed_electrostatic_potential_real_part
items.description:
Real part of the complex first-order electrostatic potential perturbation
eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability
analysis.
items.documentation:
The perturbed electrostatic potential $\delta\hat{\phi}$ is a complex
spatial eigenfunction in linear MHD stability analysis, representing the
scalar potential part of the first-order electric field perturbation
$\delta\mathbf{E} = -\nabla\delta\phi - \partial_t\delta\mathbf{A}$ for a
single toroidal Fourier mode number $n$. This quantity is the real part
$\mathrm{Re}(\delta\hat{\phi})$, encoding the in-phase component of the
eigenfunction in the poloidal plane defined by the $(R, Z)$ coordinates of
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The complex eigenfunction is fully specified by combining this quantity with
[perturbed_electrostatic_potential_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential_imaginary_part):

$$
\delta\hat{\phi}(R,Z) = \mathrm{Re}(\delta\hat{\phi}) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\delta\hat{\phi})
$$

where the physical perturbation field at toroidal angle $\phi$ is recovered
as $\mathrm{Re}[\delta\hat{\phi}(R,Z)\,e^{in\phi}]$, and $n$ is the toroidal
mode number.

The absolute amplitude and phase of the eigenfunction depend on the
normalization convention adopted by the linear stability solver; only
relative amplitudes among simultaneously computed perturbation quantities
carry physical meaning. The analogous real-part components in the same
eigenfunction family include
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part),
all resolved on the same poloidal plane for a given toroidal mode.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel-ion
pseudo-species evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal
transport barrier, where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport can
sustain steep fuel-density gradients; deuterium and tritium ions are treated
as one effective population.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel-ion
pseudo-species at the internal transport barrier is the local number density
of deuterium and tritium fuel ions treated as one effective population on
the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. The internal
transport barrier is a confined-plasma flux-surface location where locally
reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep fuel-density gradients
across neighboring flux surfaces.

The combined density is defined as the sum of the isotope ion densities at
the barrier flux surface:

$$
n_{\mathrm{DT,ITB}} = n_{\mathrm{D,ITB}} + n_{\mathrm{T,ITB}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{DT,ITB}}$ is the deuterium-tritium pseudo-species density
at the internal transport barrier, and $n_{\mathrm{D,ITB}}$ and
$n_{\mathrm{T,ITB}}$ are the deuterium and tritium ion densities at the same
barrier flux surface. This species-level number density is summed over all
charge states of deuterium and tritium ions and excludes neutral deuterium
and tritium atoms.

The deuterium-tritium pseudo-species denotes a fuel-state quantity, not a
fusion reaction rate or reaction-product population. If represented by mean
mass number $A = 2.5$, it corresponds to an equal deuterium-tritium
number-density mixture; for unequal isotope mixtures the density remains the
isotope sum, while the effective mass number is composition-weighted. It is
distinct from the isotope-resolved [deuterium density at the internal
transport barrier](name:deuterium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
[tritium density at the internal transport
barrier](name:tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), and from
spatially aggregated deuterium-tritium quantities such as [volume-averaged
deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density).

items.name: radial_ion_particle_flux
items.description:
Radial ion particle flux is the net ion crossing rate per area normal to
increasing major radius for one specified species, summed over all ionic
charge states.
items.documentation:
Radial ion particle flux is the signed net ion crossing rate per area
perpendicular to the major-radius direction for one specified species.
Crossings in opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the defining projection
is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,R} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,R}$ is the radial ion particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the ion number-flux vector, $i$ identifies the
selected ion species, and $\hat{R}$ points toward increasing major radius
$R$. The coordinate $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The flux includes thermal and nonthermal ions and is summed over all ionic
charge states of the selected species without charge weighting. It excludes
neutral particles and is not summed over ion species. It is a local
particle-number flux, not an electric-current flux or a surface-integrated
particle rate.

This quantity specializes [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux) by
fixing the oriented surface normal to $\hat{R}$. The [ion charge-state
particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) instead retains a
specified charge state. The major-radius direction generally differs from
the outward normal to a magnetic flux surface, so these two projections are
not interchangeable.

Sign convention: Positive when the net ion flow is toward increasing major
radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal lithium velocity at an internal transport barrier
is the signed toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity,
evaluated at the barrier flux-surface location. It is the density-weighted
mean over Li+ through Li3+ and is positive along increasing toroidal angle φ
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Density-weighted toroidal lithium velocity at an internal transport barrier
is the signed toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity evaluated
at the flux-surface location of that barrier. It is an intensive
species-level velocity, formed as the density-weighted mean over the lithium
ion charge states Li$^{+}$ through Li$^{3+}$.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{ITB}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the density-weighted toroidal
lithium velocity at the internal transport barrier,
$n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the number density of lithium
charge state $q+$ at that location,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the fluid velocity of that
charge state at that location, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Neutral lithium atoms are excluded from the aggregation. The value is not a
flux-surface average unless explicitly identified as such by a separate
quantity, and it is undefined where the summed lithium ion density in the
denominator is zero.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted lithium ion velocity has
a positive projection on $\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: total_ion_particle_volumetric_source_rate
items.description:
Total ion particle volumetric source rate is the net local production or
removal of ions per physical volume, summed over all ion species and ionic
charge states.
items.documentation:
Total ion particle volumetric source rate is the net local rate at which a
source contribution adds or removes ion particles per physical volume. It
contributes to the source term in the total ion number-density continuity
equation.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_i = \sum_s \sum_q \left(S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{gain}}-S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{loss}}\right)
$$

where $S_i$ is the total ion particle volumetric source rate, $s$ labels ion
species, $q$ labels ionic charge states, and $S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{gain}}$ and
$S_{s,q}^{\mathrm{loss}}$ are the local volumetric rates of particle
addition and removal for that species and charge state. The sums include all
ion species and all their ionic charge states, excluding neutral states.

The rate includes ionization, recombination, and particle exchange processes
represented by the specified source contribution. Positive values indicate
net ion gain; negative values indicate net ion loss. Transitions between
ionic charge states cancel in the total when both states are included,
whereas transitions between neutral and ionic states can change the total
ion count. This is a particle-number source, not a charge-weighted source or
the density change caused by transport-flux divergence; electron and neutral
inventories are excluded.

Its integral over the considered plasma volume gives the [total ion particle
source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate). Thus, “total” here
denotes summation over ion species and ionic charge states, not volume
integration or mandatory aggregation over independent source contributions.

items.name: capacitance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description:
Effective capacitance of an impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna, relating stored charge to the RF voltage used for circuit
tuning.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the non-negative lumped capacitance associated with an
impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron heating antenna module. It
represents the element's ability to store electric charge and participate in
tuning the radio-frequency transmission circuit.

For an ideal lumped capacitive element, the capacitance is defined by

$$
C = \frac{Q}{V}
$$

where $C$ is the capacitance, $Q$ is the charge stored on the element, and
$V$ is the electric potential difference across the element.

The quantity applies to the specified matching element of the antenna and
does not represent the capacitance of an unrelated circuit component or the
entire transmission system. It is a circuit parameter rather than a power,
current, or operating-frequency quantity.

Together with the [resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), it characterizes
the antenna's effective RF impedance; the [frequency of an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna](name:frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) identifies
the RF operating frequency at which the matching condition is evaluated.

items.name: diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity coefficient for diamagnetic, advective, non-diffusive
transport of selected momentum populations, components, and transport
directions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the diamagnetic
contribution to advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum for a
selected population, momentum component, and transport direction. It is a
transport-closure quantity, not the population’s actual bulk flow velocity.

For the selected momentum component and transport direction, the diamagnetic
convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}} = V_{\mathrm{dia}} P
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to
convective momentum flux, $V_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this convection velocity,
and $P$ is the corresponding momentum density.

This quantity isolates the diamagnetic contribution from the total momentum
convection velocity. A charge-state-resolved realization is the [ion
charge-state diamagnetic momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity),
while [diamagnetic momentum
diffusivity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity) describes the distinct
diffusive contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated diamagnetic momentum flux is
in the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported momentum
density.

items.name: beryllium_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of beryllium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over all positive ionization states.
items.documentation:
Number density of beryllium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the beryllium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local beryllium-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Be}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the number of beryllium ions in the volume, and $V$ is
a small plasma volume centered at the sheath entrance.

This quantity applies to the ionized beryllium population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target and is summed over all positive beryllium
ionization states, with each ion counted once regardless of charge state.
Neutral beryllium atoms are excluded; the quantity is a local number
density, not an areal particle flux, integrated inventory, or charge
density.

Compared with [beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density), this quantity
specifies the divertor-target sheath-entrance locus. It is distinct from
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target),
which counts free electrons rather than beryllium ions.

items.name: poloidal_length_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Poloidal arc length of a closed magnetic-flux-surface contour in an
equilibrium poloidal cross-section, measuring the perimeter of that selected
surface.
items.documentation:
The poloidal length is the perimeter of the closed contour formed by one
selected magnetic flux surface in a poloidal cross-section. It is a
geometric property of the surface boundary, rather than its enclosed area,
volume, or toroidal circumference.

The contour length is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height:

$$
L_{\mathrm{pol}} = \int_{\theta_a}^{\theta_b} \sqrt{\left(\frac{dR(\theta)}{d\theta}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{dZ(\theta)}{d\theta}\right)^2}\,d\theta
$$

Here $L_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal length, $\theta$ is any smooth
parameter along the contour, $R(\theta)$ and $Z(\theta)$ are its cylindrical
coordinate functions, and $\theta_a$ and $\theta_b$ are parameter values at
the same contour point after one complete circuit. The contour is taken at
fixed toroidal angle $\phi$.

The quantity applies to one magnetic flux surface and includes the complete
closed poloidal contour, with no averaging or summation over multiple
surfaces. It excludes local arc segments and geometric quantities associated
with the enclosed region. The selected surface may be labeled by the
[normalized poloidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate).

Unlike [elongation of a flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface),
which describes a scale-independent cross-sectional shape ratio, the
poloidal length retains the absolute geometric scale of the contour.

items.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Signed toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the radial location identified with the internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
The helium-3 ion velocity at the internal transport barrier is the
density-weighted mean fluid velocity of the helium-3 ion charge states,
excluding neutral helium-3. It is evaluated at the radial location assigned
to the internal transport barrier and is not a flux-surface average unless
separately specified.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component,
$\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion fluid velocity, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The corresponding species comparison at the same locus
is [toroidal deuterium velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
while evaluation at another characteristic location is given by [toroidal
helium-3 velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when the helium-3 ion velocity has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity
items.description:
Toroidal component of the complex first-order plasma velocity perturbation
eigenfunction in linear MHD stability analysis, encoding the amplitude and
phase of toroidal bulk plasma oscillation for a specified Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
The toroidal perturbed plasma velocity $\delta\hat{v}_\phi$ is the
projection of the complex vector eigenfunction
$\delta\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\mathbf{r})$ representing first-order oscillatory
perturbations of bulk plasma flow in linear MHD onto the $\hat{\phi}$
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. For each toroidal Fourier harmonic
$n$, this component captures how the bulk plasma oscillates along the
toroidal direction about the magnetostatic equilibrium.

As a complex scalar, it decomposes into real and imaginary parts:

$$
\delta\hat{v}_\phi(\mathbf{r}) = \mathrm{Re}[\delta\hat{v}_\phi] + i\,\mathrm{Im}[\delta\hat{v}_\phi]
$$

where $\mathrm{Re}[\delta\hat{v}_\phi]$ is given by
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part)
and $\mathrm{Im}[\delta\hat{v}_\phi]$ by
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part);
together they encode the spatial amplitude and phase of the toroidal flow
perturbation for the eigenmode.

This is the toroidal projection of the full vector eigenfunction described
by [perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:perturbed_plasma_velocity); analogous
complex structures exist for radial and poloidal projections, such as
[radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part)
and
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part).
The relative magnitudes of toroidal, poloidal, and radial components
characterize the mode polarization; the eigenfunction is evaluated by linear
MHD eigenvalue solvers applied to a reconstructed magnetostatic equilibrium.

Sign convention: Positive when $\delta\hat{v}_\phi$ points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: y_first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge
items.description:
Y-axis component of the unit vector along the first measurement axis of a
structural strain-rosette gage, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x,
y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
Y-axis component of the unit vector along the first measurement axis of a
structural strain-rosette gage is the scalar projection of that oriented
measurement-axis unit vector onto the $\hat{y}$ basis direction of the
right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y},
\hat{z})$. It is a direction cosine describing gage orientation, not a
strain value.

The component is defined by the dot product:

$$
u_{1y} = \mathbf{u}_1 \cdot \hat{y}
$$

where $u_{1y}$ is this y-axis component, $\mathbf{u}_1$ is the unit vector
along the first measurement axis of the structural strain-rosette gage, and
$\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$
frame.

Together with the corresponding x-axis component and z-axis component, it
specifies the full orientation of the first measurement axis and satisfies
the unit-vector normalization $u_{1x}^2 + u_{1y}^2 + u_{1z}^2 = 1$. It is
distinct from the y-axis component of the unit vector along the second
measurement axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the unit vector along the first measurement
axis of the structural strain-rosette gage has a component in the $+\hat{y}$
direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

items.name: linear_mhd_mode_reference_phase
items.description:
Signed angular offset that fixes the phase origin of a linear MHD eigenmode
relative to its zero-phase complex representation.
items.documentation:
A reference phase is a signed angular offset that establishes the phase
origin of a complex linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation or eigenmode.
For a vector of phase components, each component applies to the
corresponding angular dependence of the mode.

For one phase component, the offset rotates the zero-phase eigenfunction
according to

$$
\delta\mathbf{X}(\mathbf{x}) = \Re\left\{\hat{\mathbf{X}}(\mathbf{x})e^{i\phi_{\rm ref}}\right\}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{X}$ is the real perturbation, $\hat{\mathbf{X}}$ is its
zero-phase complex eigenfunction, $\phi_{\rm ref}$ is the reference phase,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $i$ is the imaginary unit, and $\Re$ denotes the
real part. The quantity is the phase offset itself, not the mode amplitude,
mode number, or oscillation frequency. Poloidal and toroidal components
share this definition; the [toroidal linear MHD mode reference
phase](name:toroidal_linear_mhd_mode_reference_phase) is a concrete toroidal
instance, while [MHD mode reference phase](name:mhd_mode_reference_phase)
denotes the broader angular reference.

Sign convention: Positive when the complex phase is advanced in the positive
angular direction of the selected mode representation relative to its
zero-phase reference; for a toroidal component, this is increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: parallel_ion_particle_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective Fickian coefficient governing down-gradient ion particle transport
along the local magnetic-field direction in the ion continuity equation.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion particle diffusivity is the effective Fickian coefficient for
particle transport along the local magnetic-field direction. It describes
the diffusive contribution to the particle flux of the ion population
represented by the ion continuity equation.

The diffusive parallel particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,\parallel} = -D_{i,\parallel}\nabla_{\parallel} n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel particle flux density of ion
species $i$, $D_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion particle diffusivity,
$\nabla_{\parallel}$ is the spatial derivative along the local
magnetic-field direction, and $n_i$ is the number density of ion species
$i$.

This quantity applies to ion particle transport only and is resolved for the
ion species represented by the continuity equation. It is not an energy or
momentum diffusivity, and it does not represent the total particle flux,
which may also contain convective or other non-diffusive contributions. The
corresponding radial coefficient [radial ion diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient) describes the analogous
particle transport across the radial direction, while [parallel ion energy
diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusivity) belongs to the distinct
energy-transport channel.

items.name: tritium_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Local particle number density of tritium ions evaluated in the boundary
plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, on the
plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
items.documentation:
Tritium density at a limiter is the local number density of tritium ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or
sheath entrance, not inside limiter material or in neutral gas at the
surface. The quantity excludes neutral tritium atoms.

Because tritium is hydrogenic, its charge-state-summed ion density is the
density of singly charged tritium ions:

$$
n_{\mathrm{T}} = n_{\mathrm{T}^{+}} = \int f_{\mathrm{T}^{+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^{3}v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the tritium ion number density,
$f_{\mathrm{T}^{+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution function of
singly charged tritium ions, and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity.

This isotope contribution is included in
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It is evaluated at a limiter
rather than at the separatrix, unlike
[tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary),
and is the tritium counterpart of
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter).

items.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the complex radial component of the linearized
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region
outside the plasma, for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD
stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The imaginary part of the complex radial vacuum magnetic-field perturbation,
$\delta B_R^{\rm im}$, is the quadrature component of the first-order
linearized magnetic-field perturbation projected along $+\hat{R}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, in the current-free vacuum
region surrounding the plasma. In linear MHD stability analysis, perturbed
fields are cast as complex Fourier harmonics in the toroidal angle $\phi$;
the imaginary part encodes the phase of the eigenmode relative to the
normalization reference, together with the [real
part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).

In the vacuum region, $\delta\mathbf{B}$ satisfies $\nabla \times
\delta\mathbf{B} = 0$ and $\nabla \cdot \delta\mathbf{B} = 0$. The complex
radial component decomposes as:

$$
\delta\tilde{B}_R^{\rm vac} = \delta B_R^{\rm re} + i\,\delta B_R^{\rm im}
$$

where $\delta B_R^{\rm re}$ is the [real
part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part) and $\delta
B_R^{\rm im}$ is this imaginary part. The perturbation amplitude is
$|\delta\tilde{B}_R^{\rm vac}| = \sqrt{(\delta B_R^{\rm re})^2 + (\delta
B_R^{\rm im})^2}$ and the phase is $\theta = \mathrm{atan2}(\delta B_R^{\rm
im},\,\delta B_R^{\rm re})$.

This quantity is computed by linear MHD stability codes for a specified
toroidal mode number $n$. Matching conditions at the plasma-vacuum interface
link it to its plasma-region counterpart, the radial plasma imaginary part.
Alongside [the toroidal vacuum imaginary
component](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), it
characterizes the helical spatial structure of the perturbed vacuum field.
As with all linear eigenfunctions, the partition between real and imaginary
parts depends on the phase normalization convention applied to the
eigenmode.

items.name: hydrogenic_density
items.description:
Charge-state- and isotope-summed number density of hydrogenic particles in
the plasma.
items.documentation:
Hydrogenic particle density is the local abundance of hydrogen isotopes,
including every included ionization state, expressed per unit volume.

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{H}} \sum_q n_{s,q}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the total hydrogenic number density, $\mathcal{H}$
is the set of included hydrogenic isotopes, $q$ indexes their charge states,
and $n_{s,q}$ is the number density of isotope $s$ in state $q$.

The quantity includes all charge states and isotopic variants and is not
restricted to a particular isotope, ionization state, or neutral population.
The concrete catalog instance is [total hydrogenic
density](name:total_hydrogenic_density).

items.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal component of the local bulk flow velocity of krypton impurity ions
at the plasma boundary, projected along the φ direction of the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is a density-weighted mean over all krypton
ionization states represented in the plasma.
items.documentation:
Toroidal component of the local bulk flow velocity of krypton impurity ions
at the plasma boundary is the projection of the krypton ion bulk-flow
velocity onto the toroidal direction at the last closed flux surface. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. As an intensive species-level
quantity, the krypton bulk-flow velocity is the density-weighted mean over
all krypton ionization states represented in the plasma.

The boundary value is defined by projecting the charge-state-averaged
krypton bulk-flow velocity onto the toroidal unit vector at the last closed
flux surface:

$$
\left. v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}} \right|_{\mathrm{LCFS}}
=
\left.
\left(
\frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}}
\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}
\right|_{\mathrm{LCFS}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the toroidal krypton bulk-flow velocity, $z$
indexes krypton ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}$ is the number
density of krypton ions in ionization state $z$,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}$ is the bulk-flow velocity vector of that
ionization state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle.

This quantity is a local boundary value, not a flux-surface average; any
flux-surface-averaged krypton boundary velocity denotes an additional
average over the last closed flux surface. The unqualified krypton species
label denotes the density-weighted mean over charge states, not a sum of
velocity components.

items.name: length_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Physical length of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the non-negative axial
extent of the probe coil along its local normal sensing axis. It
characterizes sensor geometry and effective sensing volume; magnetic-flux
sensitivity is associated with enclosed coil area and winding turn count
rather than this length alone.
items.documentation:
Physical length of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the non-negative axial
extent of the probe coil along its local normal sensing axis. The probe coil
is oriented so that its normal senses the toroidal magnetic-field component
$B_\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the
length refers to sensor geometry, not to an extent of the magnetic field.

Using projection onto the local sensing axis, the length is the span of the
active winding region along that axis:

$$
L_\phi = \max_{\mathbf{r} \in \mathcal{C}} (\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}) - \min_{\mathbf{r} \in \mathcal{C}} (\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})
$$

where $L_\phi$ is the physical length of the toroidal magnetic-field probe,
$\mathcal{C}$ is the active winding region of the probe coil, $\mathbf{r}$
is the position vector of a point in that region, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is
the normalized local normal sensing-axis direction.

This quantity applies to one physical toroidal magnetic-field probe coil; it
is not summed, averaged, or otherwise aggregated over a set of probes. As a
scalar span, it is non-negative and is not a signed displacement along
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$. It excludes the probe's [enclosed
area](name:area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), winding turn count, body
diameter, lead length, installation position, and any path length around the
device.

The product of this length with the [enclosed
area](name:area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe) characterizes the probe's
effective sensing volume. Magnetic-flux sensitivity of the pickup coil is
associated with enclosed area and winding turn count, while the [probe
voltage](name:voltage_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe) is the response
quantity produced by changing magnetic flux; the corresponding
[poloidal-probe length](name:length_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) uses
the same projected-span convention for its probe orientation.

items.name: ion_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total ion
population, aggregating both thermal and fast ion sub-populations across all
ion species and charge states without prescribing the thermal or fast
character of the receiving ions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the
complete ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with all
colliding plasma constituents. As a structural abstraction within the
collisional-power family, it aggregates thermal and fast ion receiving
populations across all ion species and charge states without resolving which
ion sub-population receives the energy.

The volume-integrated ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm ion,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm ion,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm ion,coll}$ is the local [ion power density due to
collisions](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) into the aggregate ion
receiving population and the integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

The receiving population is charge-state-summed for each ion species and
species-summed over the ion population. Collisional exchanges among ion
sub-populations contained in this aggregate cancel in the all-ion sum; the
retained value is the net transfer between the aggregate ion population and
populations outside that aggregate, including the complementary electron
power due to collisions. Population-resolved components include [fast ion
power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions), [thermal
ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions), and
the charge-state-resolved [ion-state power due to
collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions); [power due
to collisions](name:power_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding
population-abstract parent.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net
energy into the complete ion population.

items.name: parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Signed projection of the local electric field along the local magnetic-field
direction, evaluated at the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
The parallel electric field at the plasma boundary is the signed projection
of the local [electric field](name:electric_field) vector onto the local
magnetic-field direction at the last closed flux surface. It is a
point-local boundary value, distinct from the parallel flux-surface-averaged
electric field.

The defining projection is

$$
E_\parallel = \mathbf{E} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{E} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $E_\parallel$ and $\mathbf{E}$ are the parallel component and
electric-field vector in V m$^{-1}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit vector. All
quantities are evaluated at the same boundary location.

The plasma boundary is the separatrix or last closed flux surface; no
flux-surface or regional averaging is implied.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric field has a component in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: total_particle_source_rate_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
items.description:
Global rate of neutral-beam particles that traverse the plasma without
absorption, representing particle loss from the beam injection source.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the global particle loss rate caused by neutral-beam
shinethrough: injected beam neutrals that pass through the plasma without
being absorbed. It is an all-particle aggregate and represents loss from the
injected beam rather than particle creation within the plasma.

The rate is defined by integrating the local shinethrough loss-rate density
over the plasma volume:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{sh}} = \int_V S_{\mathrm{sh}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the total shinethrough particle loss rate,
$S_{\mathrm{sh}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local rate density of beam particles
not absorbed, $V$ is the plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ is position. It is
a loss magnitude, not the net balance of all plasma particle sources and
sinks. The aggregation is analogous to the global quantity [total ion
particle source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate), but the present
rate is attributed specifically to neutral-beam shinethrough.

items.name: radius_of_coil_conductor_element
items.description:
Curvature radius of a circular arc defining an active poloidal-field coil's
cross-sectional contour, evaluated at the coil conductor element.
items.documentation:
This radius specifies the bending of an individual circular arc defining the
cross-sectional contour of an active poloidal-field coil, evaluated at the
coil conductor element.

The defining relation is

$$
R = \frac{1}{\kappa}
$$

where $R$ is the arc's curvature radius and $\kappa$ is the magnitude of its
planar curvature.

The radius is constant along each circular arc and applies separately to
that arc, rather than representing an average over the contour. It describes
cross-sectional boundary curvature, not the curvature of the conductor path
around the device.

Each arc begins at a contour point and ends at the starting point of the
next arc. The [radial outline of the poloidal-field
coil](name:radial_outline_of_poloidal_field_coil) gives the major-radius
coordinates of these contour points; those coordinates locate the boundary
relative to the toroidal symmetry axis and are distinct from the arc
curvature radius.

items.name: height_of_iron_core_segment
items.description:
Height of an iron-core segment is the full, nonnegative vertical extent of
its rectangular cross-section.
items.documentation:
Height of iron core segment

The defining relation is

$$
h = Z_{\max} - Z_{\min}
$$

where $h$ is the height, and $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the vertical
coordinates of the upper and lower edges of the rectangular cross-section.

This quantity is a full dimension, not a half-height or a vertical position.
It applies to one segment rather than the complete core. The [width of the
iron-core segment](name:width_of_iron_core_segment) is the complementary
full extent along the major-radius direction.

items.name: tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the tritium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tritium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all tritium ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the tritium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tritium-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents tritium ions specifically, rather than electrons,
other ion species, neutral tritium, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{T,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{T}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{T,axis}}$ is the tritium-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the number of tritium ions, and $V$ is
physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete tritium-ion population at that location
and is summed over all tritium ionic charge states; neutral tritium is
excluded. It is neither a flux-surface nor a volume integral.

This is the tritium-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [tritium density at the plasma
boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which describes the same
charge-state aggregation at the plasma boundary rather than at the magnetic
axis.

items.name: explicit_ion_torque
items.description:
Volume-integrated explicit torque vector acting on the combined ion
population, summed over ion species and charge states and independent of the
primary transported momentum variable.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the global explicit source or sink of angular momentum for
the combined ion population, represented as a torque vector integrated over
the relevant plasma volume. It retains the full directional torque rather
than selecting a single cylindrical component.

The volume-integrated torque is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{T}_{i,\mathrm{exp}} = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\boldsymbol{T}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}$ is the explicit ion torque vector,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{exp}}$ is the corresponding local
torque-density vector, $V$ is the relevant plasma volume, and $\mathrm{d}V$
is its volume element. The subscript $i$ denotes the combined ion
population, and $\mathrm{exp}$ denotes the explicit source contribution.

The quantity applies globally to all included ion species and ionic charge
states, which are summed rather than represented separately. It is
independent of the primary transported momentum variable and excludes any
torque contribution defined solely through that variable; it is also
distinct from a local torque density and from a single-direction projection.

The broader [ion torque](name:ion_torque) is the net volume-integrated
torque on the ion population, while [toroidal explicit ion
torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque) is the toroidal projection of
this explicit vector contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when each vector component points in its
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is increasing toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of charged ions at the plasma boundary, with each
specialization defining whether the value is local or averaged over the last
closed magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Number density of ions at the plasma boundary is the particle count per
physical volume for a charged-ion population associated with the last closed
magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.

The defining charge-state-summed velocity-space moment is

$$
n_i(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{Z>0}\int f_{s,Z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the
plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of included ion
species, $Z$ is a positive ionic charge state, $f_{s,Z}$ is the velocity
distribution function of species $s$ in charge state $Z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The aggregation is additive over the included charged-ion species and all
their positive charge states; neutral atoms are excluded. A concrete
instance may provide the local boundary value, as in [total ion density at
the plasma boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), or its
average over the last closed magnetic flux surface, as in
[flux-surface-averaged ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary). This
ion-specific parent is narrower than [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose selected population and
neutral-particle inclusion are specialization-dependent.

items.name: poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective coefficient multiplying the poloidal gradient in diffusive
transport of total bulk-flow momentum within the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective diffusivity governing diffusive transport of
the aggregate bulk-flow momentum in the local poloidal direction within the
edge plasma.

Its relation to the directional momentum-diffusivity tensor is

$$
