D_{\mathrm{pol}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}} \cdot \mathbf D_{\mathrm{mom}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $D_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal diffusion coefficient,
$\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local unit vector in the poloidal
direction, and $\mathbf D_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is the effective diffusivity
tensor for total bulk-flow momentum; the dot products denote tensor
contraction.

The total designation means that this coefficient applies to the aggregate
momentum balance without selecting an ion species, ion charge state, or
neutral state. It is restricted to the poloidal transport direction and the
edge-plasma region; it does not represent a species-resolved coefficient or
a coefficient for another transport direction.

This quantity is the poloidal component of the directional coefficient
vector represented by [total momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). It is distinct from
[poloidal ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), which
applies only to ion momentum transport, and from [poloidal neutral-state
momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_diffusivity),
which applies only to neutral-state momentum transport.

items.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal fluid velocity of hydrogen ions at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along increasing toroidal angle in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion fluid velocity component tangent to the
toroidal direction at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier. It describes the directed bulk motion of the hydrogen-ion
population, rather than its speed or a thermal velocity spread.

$$
v_{\phi,H} = \mathbf{v}_H \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_H$ is the hydrogen-ion fluid-velocity vector and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The pedestal-top locus denotes the inner shoulder of
the edge transport barrier and is distinct from the hydrogen-ion velocity
evaluated at an internal transport barrier, as in
[toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
The quantity is a directed component, not the magnitude of the hydrogen-ion
velocity.

Sign convention: Positive when the hydrogen-ion fluid velocity points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: total_implicit_ion_particle_source_rate
items.description:
Total implicit ion particle source rate is the coefficient multiplying total
ion number density in the density-proportional contribution to its
particle-number source.
items.documentation:
Total implicit ion particle source rate is the coefficient of the
density-proportional, implicit contribution to the total-ion particle-number
source. It multiplies total ion number density in the decomposed density
transport equation.

The source decomposition is defined by

$$
S_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = S_{i,\mathrm{exp}}^{\mathrm{tot}} + S_{i,\mathrm{imp}}^{\mathrm{tot}} n_i^{\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the net total-ion particle source per physical
volume, $S_{i,\mathrm{exp}}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its explicit contribution,
$S_{i,\mathrm{imp}}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is this implicit source coefficient, and
$n_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is total ion number density. The explicit contribution
is independent of the density being advanced within this decomposition; the
implicit contribution is the coefficient multiplied by that density.

Total ion number density is summed over all included ion species and ionic
charge states, counting ions without charge weighting and excluding
electrons and neutral particles. The coefficient acts on this aggregate
density; it is not itself the full volumetric source or a volume-integrated
particle production rate.

This quantity is the total-ion specialization of the [implicit ion particle
source rate](name:implicit_ion_particle_source_rate). In contrast, the
[implicit ion-state particle source
rate](name:implicit_ion_state_particle_source_rate) multiplies the density
of a specified ion state rather than the aggregate ion density.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-proportional contribution adds
ions to the total ion population; negative values represent removal.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Field-aligned projection of the pressure-gradient diamagnetic fluid velocity
of one ion charge state in the edge plasma, identically zero because this
drift is perpendicular to the magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the local
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma onto the magnetic-field direction. It represents a
fluid-moment contribution rather than the guiding-center motion of
individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state with scalar partial pressure, the defining
projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\parallel} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}} = 0
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the specified ion charge state,
$v_{\ast\alpha,\parallel}$ is its field-parallel diamagnetic-drift velocity
component, $p_\alpha$ is its partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its
pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector,
$B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge,
$n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow. Its vanishing value follows from the perpendicularity of the
pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift, not from the absence of total parallel
ion flow.

The [perpendicular ion charge-state velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
instead resolves the same drift along a specified local direction
perpendicular to the magnetic field and need not vanish. The species-level
[ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted
mean over all ionic charge states of that species, not their sum; its
parallel projection therefore also vanishes for this pressure-gradient
drift.

items.name: xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
items.documentation:
Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary is the amount of the
xenon ion population per physical volume at the last closed magnetic flux
surface. It is the local boundary value, not a flux-surface average.

The local charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{54}\int f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the xenon ion charge-state
number, $f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}$ is the velocity distribution function for charge
state $Z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. The aggregation is additive over all xenon ion charge
states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral
xenon atoms. The value is local at the boundary rather than averaged over
that surface.

This entry specializes the population-unspecified
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to xenon ions.
The corresponding flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
applies the same xenon charge-state aggregation after averaging over the
plasma-boundary flux surface, so it is distinct from this local quantity.

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Signed coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror along its second local tangential axis in its object-local
planar frame, measured from the mirror-local origin.
items.documentation:
Signed coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror along its second local tangential axis in its object-local
planar frame, measured from the mirror-local origin, is the scalar
projection of that point's displacement onto the mirror's second local
tangential direction. The mirror-local triad is
$(\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{n}})$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$ is the more-horizontal tangential direction directed
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height;
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the plasma-facing unit normal; and
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\times\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$ completes the
right-handed triad.

For an outline point with position vector $\mathbf{r}$ and mirror-local
origin $\mathbf{r}_0$, the coordinate is defined by

$$
x_2 = \left(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_0\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2
$$

where $x_2$ is the second local tangential coordinate of the outline point.

This coordinate specifies the second in-plane component of the mirror
outline and complements the [first local tangential
coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
It is not the cylindrical radial coordinate $R$, toroidal angle $\phi$, or
vertical coordinate $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the mirror-local origin
to the outline point has a component in the direction
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\times\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$.

items.name: momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Diamagnetic-drift contribution to an area-normalized momentum-balance
source, representing pressure-gradient-driven transport of a specified
projected linear momentum.
items.documentation:
Diamagnetic-drift contribution to an area-normalized momentum-balance source
is the part of the source for a specified projected linear momentum caused
by pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport in a magnetized plasma. It
represents the net effect of the diamagnetic projected-momentum stress on
the momentum balance after normalization by the area through which the
balance is written.

An area-normalized source is defined from the corresponding volumetric
projected-momentum source density over a balance volume:

$$
S_{\mathrm{mom,dia}} = \frac{1}{A}\int_V q_{\mathrm{mom,dia}}\,dV,\qquad q_{\mathrm{mom,dia}}=-\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{mom,dia}}$ is the area-normalized diamagnetic-drift
momentum source, $A$ is the normalizing area, $V$ is the balance volume,
$q_{\mathrm{mom,dia}}$ is the volumetric projected-momentum source density
with dimensions of force per volume, and $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{dia}}$
is the diamagnetic projected-momentum flux tensor with dimensions of force
per area. The division by $A$ makes this quantity area-normalized rather
than a volumetric force density; the minus sign follows the conservation-law
convention that an outward divergence of momentum flux is a sink.

This quantity is the momentum-specific member of
source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift. It differs from
[momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift),
which is the flux or stress before taking its divergence and area
normalization, and it is not the effective transport coefficient
[diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity).
The scalar projection is a projected linear-momentum component; an
angular-momentum moment arm or torque normalization is not implied.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic-drift term increases the
projected linear momentum in the positive direction of the momentum
projection used in the balance.

items.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Net torque about the toroidal symmetry axis transferred to thermal ions by
collisional momentum exchange.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net toroidal angular-momentum transfer to the
thermal-ion population from colliding particle populations, integrated over
the plasma volume. It represents torque about the toroidal symmetry axis
rather than a local torque density.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi,i}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V R\,\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},i}\cdot\hat{\phi}\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi,i}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the integrated collisional
torque, $V$ is the plasma volume, $R$ is major radius in m,
$\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},i}$ is the collisional force density on thermal
ions in N m$^{-3}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$. The thermal-ion contribution is summed
over all represented thermal-ion charge states; its local
charge-state-resolved counterpart is [toroidal thermal-ion charge-state
torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the collisional force on thermal ions has a
component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, producing
positive angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Outgoing neutral internal-state particle number flux density at a
plasma-facing wall due to recombination, resolved by neutral product species
and internal quantum state.
items.documentation:
Outgoing neutral internal-state particle number flux density at a
plasma-facing wall due to recombination is the surface flux density of
neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state that are
produced by recombination at the wall and cross the wall surface away from
the wall. It is resolved by neutral product species and by the internal
quantum state of that product.

For neutral product species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, with
$\hat{\mathbf n}_w$ the unit normal directed from the wall material into the
adjacent plasma, the outgoing recombination contribution is defined by

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{rec,out}}_{n,\alpha} = \int_{\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w > 0} (\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w)\, f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}(\mathbf v)\, d^3\mathbf v
$$

where $\mathbf v$ is neutral-particle velocity and
$f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}$ is the velocity-space distribution function at
the wall for neutral recombination products of species $n$ in internal state
$\alpha$, normalized so that its velocity integral gives the corresponding
local neutral-product number density.

This quantity includes only the emitted, outward wall-normal component of
neutral recombination products in the specified internal state. Aggregating
over internal states for the same neutral product species gives the [neutral
particle flux at wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); the
broader internal-state-resolved recombination-flux family is internal state
particle flux at wall due to recombination. The distinct inward wall-normal
counterpart is [incident neutral internal-state particle flux at wall due to
recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination)
and is not included here.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral recombination products cross the wall
surface in the direction of the wall normal from the wall material into the
adjacent plasma.

items.name: total_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of
total plasma momentum, distinct from the plasma bulk flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective,
non-diffusive transport of total plasma momentum for a selected momentum
component and transport direction. It is a transport closure quantity, not
an actual plasma bulk flow velocity.

For each selected total-momentum component and transport direction, the
convective total-momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}} P_\mathrm{tot}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding
convective flux of total plasma momentum, $V_{\mathrm{tot},\mathrm{conv}}$
is the total momentum convection velocity, and $P_\mathrm{tot}$ is the
corresponding total plasma momentum density. The definition applies
componentwise when the momentum component or transport direction is
resolved.

The scope is total plasma momentum only; it does not denote
species-resolved, charge-state-resolved, neutral-only, or
attributed-contribution momentum convection velocities. A resolved
projection of this quantity is the [parallel total momentum convection
velocity](name:parallel_total_momentum_convection_velocity).

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective total-momentum flux
is in the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported
total-momentum density.

items.name: count_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Count of discrete toroidal-field-coil modules forming the device’s toroidal
magnetic-field system; conductor turns within a module are not counted
separately.
items.documentation:
The toroidal-field-coil module count is the number of distinct coil modules
forming the device’s toroidal magnetic-field system. Each module is counted
once, regardless of how many conductor turns or conductor elements it
contains.

This count is an inventory of coil modules, not a winding-turn count and not
a measure of electrical excitation or conductor geometry. Those properties
are described separately by the [current of a toroidal field
coil](name:current_of_toroidal_field_coil) and the [area of a toroidal field
coil](name:area_of_toroidal_field_coil).

items.name: vertical_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of vertical momentum
carried by one neutral species, aggregated over neutral states. Vertical
denotes the momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame, not velocity direction.
items.documentation:
Vertical neutral species momentum convection velocity is the
flux-surface-normal convection coefficient that multiplies the vertical
momentum density carried by neutrals of one chemical species. The vertical
momentum component is defined along $hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height; the coefficient itself is not a velocity
directed along $hat{Z}$. It is the vertical component of the [neutral
species momentum convection
velocity](name:neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity).

The defining relation preserves the total convective flux of vertical
momentum across a magnetic flux surface:

$$
\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = P_{Z,a} V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_{s \in a} P_{Z,s} V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ denotes one neutral chemical species, $s$ runs over its resolved
neutral states, $P_{Z,s}$ and $P_{Z,a}$ are signed vertical momentum
densities, $V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ are
state-resolved and species-aggregated convection coefficients, and
$\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum
flux. The state sum excludes other chemical species and this local
coefficient is not a flux-surface average. Unlike [vertical neutral
velocity](name:vertical_neutral_velocity), it is defined by momentum
transport.

Sign convention: Positive when $\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $P_{Z,a}$
have the same sign, with positive vertical momentum directed toward
increasing $Z$ and positive flux-surface-normal transport directed toward
increasing magnetic flux label.

items.name: incident_thermal_power_at_wall
items.description:
Thermal power carried from the plasma and incident on the first wall,
defining the wall-directed heat load before downstream coolant extraction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the thermal power transported from the plasma toward and
incident on the first wall. It represents an integrated wall load rather
than a local heat-flux density.

The incident thermal power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{wall}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{th,inc}}}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the thermal power incident on the first wall
and $E_{\mathrm{th,inc}}$ is the thermal energy delivered from the plasma to
the wall.

The quantity applies to the thermal plasma contribution and aggregates the
incident power over the first-wall surface. It excludes power extracted by
coolant after deposition and is distinct from [total thermal
coolant-absorbed power at the
wall](name:total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall), which describes
the downstream removal of deposited energy. It is also not limited to the
radiative component represented by [absorbed radiated power at the
wall](name:absorbed_radiated_power_at_wall).

The total incident load can contain conductive and convective contributions,
represented by [power due to conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction) and
[power due to convection](name:power_due_to_convection) when those
components are resolved.

items.name: ion_charge_state_average_charge_number
items.description:
Concentration-weighted mean ionic charge number within a specified
charge-state bundle of one ion species, expressing the bundle's mean
ionization state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the mean ionic charge number of a specified charge-state
bundle of one ion species. It is the bundle-restricted instance of [average
charge number](name:average_charge_number).

The concentration-weighted mean is defined by

$$
\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}} = \frac{\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} q\,n_q}{\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} n_q}
$$

where $\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the bundle's mean charge number,
$\mathcal{B}$ is the set of charge states included in the bundle, $q$ is the
integer ionic charge number, and $n_q$ is the number density of ions in
charge state $q$. The denominator is the total number density within the
bundle and must be nonzero.

The mean includes all charge states represented by the specified bundle, but
not states outside it or other ion species. It is a normalized,
number-density-weighted mean, not a sum of charge numbers. For a bundle
containing one charge state, it equals that state's charge number. It
differs from the [mean squared charge
number](name:square_of_ion_charge_state_charge_number), which averages
squared charge numbers rather than charge numbers.

The [volume-averaged ion charge-state average charge
number](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number) is the
plasma-volume mean of this local bundle quantity. Spatial averaging is an
additional operation and is not part of the charge-state averaging defined
here.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Dimensionless magnetic-surface coordinate locating the internal transport
barrier between the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
The normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier is
the dimensionless magnetic-surface label assigned to the flux surface
containing the barrier. It locates that surface within the nested
closed-flux region rather than giving a cylindrical distance or vector
component.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ITB}) = \left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{ITB}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,LCFS}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right]^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ITB})$ is the normalized toroidal
flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{ITB})$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed
by the flux surface containing the barrier, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is
its value at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,LCFS}}$ is its value
at the last closed flux surface. The nonnegative square-root branch is used.

The value applies specifically to the flux surface assigned to the internal
transport barrier and is bounded from zero at the magnetic axis to unity at
the last closed flux surface for nested surfaces with monotonic toroidal
flux. It has no species, charge-state, or spatial averaging; it is a scalar
surface label.

This quantity is the internal-transport-barrier specialization of the
[normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike the [toroidal
flux coordinate at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier), it
uses axis-to-last-closed-flux-surface normalization and is therefore
dimensionless.

items.name: current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
items.description:
Vector conventional electric current density attributable to non-inductive
wave–particle interactions, represented locally or after averaging over
magnetic flux surfaces.
items.documentation:
Wave-driven current density is the conventional electric-current-density
vector attributable to electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions that drive
plasma current non-inductively. It represents charge transport in the plasma
rather than the total current carried by an external circuit.

Its population-resolved definition is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{w}} = \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{w}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{w}}$ is the wave-driven electric current-density
vector, $s$ indexes the contributing charged plasma populations, $q_s$ is
the signed charge of population $s$, and
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{w}}$ is that population's particle-flux
vector attributable to wave-driven current drive.

The species sum aggregates the charged plasma populations contributing to
the wave-driven current, while spatial, flux-surface, or mode aggregation
depends on the representation. The quantity excludes inductive current and
current driven by non-wave mechanisms; it is a current density, not a
volume-integrated net plasma current.

The [current density per toroidal mode due to wave-driven current
drive](name:current_density_per_toroidal_mode_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
is a representation that retains toroidal-mode resolution, whereas the
[flux-surface-averaged current density due to wave-driven current
drive](name:flux_surface_averaged_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
applies a magnetic flux-surface average. The related [current due to
wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
represents the corresponding net plasma-current quantity obtained from the
appropriate integration or projection of this density.

items.name: ion_momentum_source
items.description:
Ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge
states.
items.documentation:
Ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge
states. It retains the direction of the net transfer rather than reducing it
to a magnitude.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
\mathbf{S}_{i} = \sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{i}} \mathbf{S}_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i}$ is the total-ion momentum source vector, $z$ indexes
the ion charge states in the set $\mathcal{Z}_{i}$, and $\mathbf{S}_{i,z}$
is the corresponding source for one charge state. The [momentum
source](name:momentum_source) defines this same directional
momentum-transfer concept at the general species and projection level.

This quantity includes all ion charge states and excludes neutral species.
It is distinct from the [ion charge-state momentum
source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which resolves one state;
its axis and field-aligned projections are components of the same total-ion
vector, including the [parallel net ion momentum
source](name:parallel_net_ion_momentum_source).

Sign convention: Positive when a projected component points along its
defined positive direction—$+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; flux-coordinate
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ and field-parallel projections use their stated
positive directions.

items.name: radial_electron_convection_velocity
items.description:
Signed major-radius component of the effective velocity multiplying electron
number density in the advective part of electron-particle transport.
items.documentation:
Radial electron convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the
density-proportional advective electron particle flux. It represents
directed convection after density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has
been separated.

The radial convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_e v_{e,R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the major-radius component of
electron particle flux due to convection, $n_e$ is electron number density,
and $v_{e,R}$ is this radial convection velocity.

The quantity applies to the electron particle channel, not to ion or neutral
transport, and is not a sum over species. It is the radial component in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius
measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height. This major-radius direction is not generally normal to a
magnetic flux surface.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven transport, whose radial
coefficient is the [radial effective electron
diffusivity](name:radial_effective_electron_diffusivity), and need not equal
the radial bulk electron flow velocity. It specializes [electron convection
velocity] by specifying the major-radius projection; [electron particle
convection velocity](name:electron_particle_convection_velocity) is the
corresponding unprojected vector coefficient.

Sign convention: Positive when the electron convective velocity points
toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: height_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Full physical extent of a rectangular neutron-detector aperture along its
second local tangential direction, the X2 axis of the detector-local
Cartesian frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the full end-to-end extent of a rectangular neutron-detector
aperture along its second local tangential direction. This direction is the
$X_2$ axis of the detector-local Cartesian basis $(\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2)$.

The extent is defined by the separation of the two boundary coordinates
along $X_2$:

$$
H_2 = X_{2,\max} - X_{2,\min}
$$

where $X_{2,\max}$ and $X_{2,\min}$ are the maximum and minimum
aperture-boundary coordinates along $X_2$, and $H_2$ is the resulting
length.

This quantity describes the second local tangential dimension and is
distinct from the [width of the neutron
detector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_diagnostic_aperture), which
measures the corresponding first local tangential dimension. For a circular
aperture, the radial size is instead characterized by the [radius of the
neutron detector](name:radius_of_neutron_detector).

items.name: square_of_major_radius
items.description:
Geometric equilibrium coefficient with inverse-square major-radius scaling,
spanning direct reciprocal-square factors and flux-coordinate metric ratios
in toroidal plasma geometry.
items.documentation:
This quantity is a geometric coefficient in toroidal plasma equilibrium
whose scale contains the reciprocal square of the [major
radius](name:major_radius). It includes both direct inverse-square radius
factors and geometric factors formed from a flux-coordinate gradient divided
by the squared major radius.

Its common form is

$$
G = \frac{g}{R^2}
$$

where $G$ is the geometric coefficient, $R$ is the major radius, and $g$ is
a dimensionless geometric factor. For
[inverse_of_square_of_major_radius](name:inverse_of_square_of_major_radius),
$g=1$; for
[ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius](name:ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius),
$g$ is the squared magnitude of the gradient of the toroidal flux
coordinate.

The quantity is a metric factor for flux-coordinate equilibrium and
transport formulations, not the major radius or its square itself. Its
specific numerator is determined by the concrete member of this
geometric-coefficient family.

items.name: x_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid
items.description:
Signed Cartesian x coordinate of a ferritic element’s geometric centroid in
the right-handed (x, y, z) frame, with z aligned with the vertical Z
direction.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed Cartesian x position of the geometric centroid of
a ferritic element. It gives the element’s absolute position in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}$
aligned with the vertical direction; it is not a radial coordinate or a
local displacement.

For an element occupying volume $V$, the centroid coordinate is defined by

$$
x_c = \frac{1}{V}\int_V x\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $x_c$ and $x$ are Cartesian x coordinates in meters, $V$ is the
element volume, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is a volume element. Together with the [y
coordinate of the ferritic element
centroid](name:y_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid) and [z coordinate
of the ferritic element
centroid](name:z_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid), it locates the
same geometric centroid; it is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the
ferritic element
centroid](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid).

Sign convention: Positive when the centroid lies in the $+x$ direction from
the Cartesian origin.

items.name: alpha_angle_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Signed inclination of the first side of a plasma-filament oblique
cross-section, measured counterclockwise from the outward radial direction
in the poloidal plane.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed inclination of the first side of the oblique
parallelogram representing an individual plasma-filament cross section. It
specifies the orientation of that side in the poloidal plane relative to the
outward radial direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the angle is
defined by

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}\left(\mathbf{a}_1\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_Z,\,\mathbf{a}_1\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_R\right)
$$

where $\alpha$ is the first-side inclination, $\mathbf{a}_1$ is the directed
vector along the first parallelogram side, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_R$ is the
outward radial unit vector in the direction of increasing $R$,
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_Z$ is the positive vertical unit vector, and
$\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the signed angle from the radial projection
toward the vertical projection.

The quantity applies separately to each discrete plasma-carrying filament
and is not an aggregate orientation averaged over the plasma. It describes
only the first side of the oblique cross section; it is not the inclination
of the second side or either side length.

The companion [tilt angle of a plasma
filament](name:tilt_angle_of_plasma_filament) specifies the inclination of
the other parallelogram side, while the [major length of a plasma
filament](name:major_length_of_plasma_filament) and [minor length of a
plasma filament](name:minor_length_of_plasma_filament) specify
cross-sectional dimensions. Together these geometric quantities define the
filament cross-section orientation and shape.

Sign convention: Positive when the directed first side is rotated
counterclockwise from the outward radial direction toward the positive
vertical direction in the poloidal plane.

items.name: ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Kinetic energy flux density carried by ions leaving the plasma-facing wall
through surface emission processes such as physical sputtering and ion
backscattering.
items.documentation:
The kinetic energy flux density at the plasma-facing wall surface carried by
ions emitted outward via surface emission — the family of plasma–wall
interaction processes, including physical sputtering, chemical sputtering,
and ion backscattering, that return ionic species from the wall to the
plasma. The `kinetic` qualifier restricts this to translational kinetic
energy of the emitted ion velocity distribution, excluding potential energy
stored in electronic excitation or residual ionization charge, which is
captured separately by
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

The emitted kinetic energy flux $\Phi_{\mathrm{kin,emit}}$ sums over all
emitted ion species $s$:

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{kin,emit}} = \sum_s \int_{v_n > 0} \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2 \, v_n \, f_{s,\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion mass of species $s$, $v = |\mathbf{v}|$ is the ion
speed, $v_n > 0$ is the outward surface-normal velocity component at the
wall, and $f_{s,\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution
function of emitted ions.

In plasma–surface interaction modeling, this flux is evaluated by convolving
incident plasma conditions with energy-resolved surface emission yields and
backscattering coefficients from binary-collision approximation databases.
It is the mechanism-attributed form of ion_energy_flux_at_wall and the
emitted counterpart to
[ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall),
which captures the incident kinetic flux. Charge-state-resolved
contributions are tracked by ion_state_energy_flux_at_wall, and the electron
analog is
[electron_energy_flux_at_wall](name:electron_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).

items.name: ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature
items.description:
Ratio of electron temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average
inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, expressing central
electron-temperature peaking.
items.documentation:
Ratio of electron temperature at the magnetic axis to its volume average
inside the last closed magnetic flux surface. It expresses central
electron-temperature peaking relative to the enclosed plasma's mean thermal
state.

It is defined by

$$\langle f\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V f\,dV$$

where $P_{T_e}$ is the electron-temperature peaking ratio,
$T_{e,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [electron temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis), and $\langle
T_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature). The volume average
is $\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV$, where $T_e$ is the
local electron kinetic temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the
last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is a physical volume element.

The denominator is weighted by physical volume, not by electron density, and
is not a flux-surface average. The numerator is evaluated at the magnetic
axis rather than at an independently located temperature maximum. The ratio
requires a positive denominator and is not an absolute temperature; unity
means that the axis temperature equals the volume average, while values
greater than unity indicate central peaking relative to that average.

The [corresponding ion-temperature
ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature)
applies the same axis-to-volume-average comparison to ion temperature.

$$a/b$$

items.name: co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description:
Co-passing torque density due to j cross b force is the vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force acting on the
co-passing plasma population. It is the parent concept for co-passing
directionally projected forms.
items.documentation:
Co-passing torque density due to $j \times B$ force is the vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force density acting on
the co-passing plasma population. Co-passing particles are passing-orbit
particles whose guiding-center motion belongs to the branch circulating
around the torus in the same sense as the plasma current. It represents the
co-passing electromagnetic torque density before any directional projection
is applied.

The vector torque density for the co-passing population is defined as the
moment of its $j \times B$ force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{r}(\mathbf{x}) \times \left[\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) \times \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}$ is the co-passing torque
density due to the $j \times B$ force, $\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from
the chosen torque reference point to position $\mathbf{x}$,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the electric current density associated with
co-passing particles, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field.

This parent quantity is already restricted to the co-passing orbit class; it
is distinct from the orbit-unrestricted [torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force). A specialized co-passing
name may add a component and flux-surface averaging, such as [toroidal
co-passing torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force),
whose toroidal projection is onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$
increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is
vertical height. [Counter-passing torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and
[trapped torque density due to $j \times B$
force](name:trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) refer to
different orbit-class populations, not components of this co-passing
quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}$ points in the positive
direction of its stated basis vector; for a toroidal projection this is
$+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: helium_confinement_time
items.description:
Characteristic e-folding time for the loss of confined thermalized helium-4
ash ions when their outward loss rate is proportional to the confined
inventory.
items.documentation:
The global particle confinement time of thermalized helium-4 ash is the
characteristic retention timescale for fully ionized helium-4 ions in the
confined plasma. It describes particle loss from the total confined
inventory, rather than the confinement of thermal energy or the survival of
the plasma as a whole.

For source-free decay, the confinement time is defined by

$$
\frac{dN_{\mathrm{He}}}{dt}=-\frac{N_{\mathrm{He}}}{\tau_{\mathrm{p,He}}}, \qquad \tau_{\mathrm{p,He}}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{He}}}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{He,loss}}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{He}}$ is the total confined helium-4 ion inventory, $t$ is
time, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{He,loss}}$ is the corresponding outward
particle-loss rate. The definition assumes loss proportional to inventory
and excludes helium sources during the decay interval. It is distinct from
[energy confinement time](name:energy_confinement_time) and plasma
confinement time.

items.name: ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-R flux
density of toroidal linear momentum for the ion population, attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
items.documentation:
Ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-$R$
flux density of toroidal linear momentum carried by the ion population and
associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The
transported momentum is the $\hat{\phi}$ component and the flux direction is
$\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The diamagnetic contribution is defined by summing the charge-state
contributions to the toroidal momentum flux:

$$
\Pi_{R\phi,i}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \sum_{\alpha} m_i n_{i,\alpha} u_{\phi,i,\alpha} v_{R,i,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $\Pi_{R\phi,i}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux, $\alpha$ labels
the included charge states, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_{i,\alpha}$ is the
charge-state number density, $u_{\phi,i,\alpha}$ is its toroidal flow
velocity, and $v_{R,i,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is its cylindrical-$R$
diamagnetic-drift velocity.

This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [momentum flux due to
diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and is
charge-state aggregated, whereas [ion charge state momentum flux due to
diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) retains
one charge state. It excludes momentum-flux contributions from
non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms.

Sign convention: Positive when positive toroidal linear momentum is
transported toward increasing $R$.

items.name: poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side
items.description:
Poloidal electron beta at the high-field-side pedestal top is the ratio of
local electron thermal pressure to magnetic pressure based on the local
poloidal magnetic-field magnitude.
items.documentation:
Poloidal electron beta at the high-field-side pedestal top compares local
electron thermal pressure with the magnetic-pressure scale associated with
the local poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. It is an electron-pressure
specialization of [plasma beta](name:beta) with a poloidal-field reference.

The defining local pressure ratio is

$$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$

where $\beta_{e,\mathrm{p,HFS}}$ denotes this poloidal electron beta,
$p_{e,\mathrm{ped,HFS}}$ is the local electron thermal pressure at the
high-field-side pedestal top, $B_{\mathrm{p,ped,HFS}}$ is the poloidal
magnetic-field magnitude at the same point, and $\mu_0$ is the vacuum
permeability.

Both inputs are point-local; neither flux-surface nor volume averaging is
applied. The numerator excludes ion pressure, and the magnetic-pressure
scale uses the poloidal field rather than the total magnetic-field
magnitude. The ratio is defined only for nonzero poloidal magnetic-field
magnitude.

It differs from [poloidal electron beta at the low-field-side pedestal
top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side) by its
evaluation locus. It also differs from [poloidal flux-surface-averaged
electron beta at the pedestal
top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_flux_surface_averaged_at_pedestal_top),
which uses flux-surface-averaged pressure and field rather than point-local
inputs, and from [poloidal beta](name:poloidal_beta), which uses a
whole-plasma total-pressure convention.

items.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective kinematic coefficient governing diffusive redistribution of an ion
species’ poloidal bulk-flow momentum, with all ionic charge states included.
items.documentation:
Poloidal ion momentum diffusivity is the effective kinematic transport
coefficient governing diffusive redistribution of the poloidal component of
ion bulk-flow [momentum](name:momentum). The poloidal direction is tangent
to a magnetic flux surface within a constant-toroidal-angle plane in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local, one-direction viscous closure, the diffusive flux of poloidal
momentum is:

$$
\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\varrho_i\chi_{i,\mathrm{p}}\frac{\partial u_{i,\mathrm{p}}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $i$ identifies the selected ion species, $\mathrm{p}$ denotes its
poloidal momentum component, $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
diffusive flux of that component along the transport direction, $\varrho_i$
is the species mass density summed over all ionic charge states,
$\chi_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is this diffusivity, $u_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is the
density-weighted mean poloidal velocity over all ionic charge states, and
$\ell$ is physical distance along the transport direction.

The poloidal qualifier selects the transported momentum component; it does
not require the transport direction to follow a poloidal arc. This kinematic
closure acts on the poloidal velocity gradient rather than the gradient of
total momentum density. It excludes convective momentum transport, residual
stress, and external momentum sources.

This quantity specializes [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity)
to the poloidal momentum of one ion species, without summing over different
ion species or including electrons or neutrals. It is a species-level
effective coefficient, not a sum of charge-state diffusivities; [poloidal
ion charge-state momentum diffusivity] instead applies to ions in one
specified ionization state.

items.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction
items.description:
Thermal power deposited on all divertor targets by parallel electron and ion
heat conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines, excluding
convective, radiative, and neutral-particle channels.
items.documentation:
The power of the divertor due to conduction is the total thermal energy
deposited on all divertor target surfaces by electron and ion heat
conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines. It excludes
convective particle enthalpy, absorbed radiation, recombination, and
neutral-particle contributions, and is the divertor-wide counterpart of
[power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction).

The total conductive power is defined by integrating the conductive
heat-flux vector over every wetted divertor target surface:

$$
P_{\mathrm{div,cond}} = \sum_k \int_{A_k} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_k\,dA
$$

where $A_k$ is the wetted surface of target $k$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_k$ points
from the plasma toward the target material, and $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}}$
is the sum of the electron and ion conductive heat-flux vectors. This
aggregate quantity covers the complete divertor assembly and is a
locus-specific component of
[power_due_to_conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), rather than the
global wall quantity
[power_at_wall_due_to_conduction](name:power_at_wall_due_to_conduction).

items.name: radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective Fickian coefficient for radial diffusive transport of thermal
energy by ions in a specified charge state.
items.documentation:
The radial ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient is the effective
proportionality coefficient for down-gradient diffusive transport of thermal
energy carried by ions in a specified charge state. It characterizes the
radial transport component directed outward from the magnetic axis.

The diffusive radial ion-energy flux is defined by

$$
q_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{diff,rad}} = -n_{i,z} D_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{rad}} \nabla_{\mathrm{rad}} T_{i,z}
$$

where $q_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{diff,rad}}$ is the radial diffusive thermal-energy
flux, $n_{i,z}$ is the number density of ion charge state $z$,
$D_{i,z,E}^{\mathrm{rad}}$ is this coefficient, $T_{i,z}$ is the
corresponding ion temperature, and $\nabla_{\mathrm{rad}}$ denotes the
outward radial gradient.

This quantity is the radial specialization of the [thermal ion charge-state
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It
applies to one specified charge state and excludes parallel, poloidal, and
toroidal transport contributions.

items.name: current_due_to_lower_hybrid_current_drive
items.description:
Net toroidal plasma current driven non-inductively by lower-hybrid slow
waves through wave–particle interactions, contributing to the total
non-inductive current.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net toroidal plasma current attributable to
lower-hybrid current drive. It represents the lower-hybrid contribution to
the plasma current and excludes inductive current and non-wave-driven
non-inductive contributions.

$$
I_{\mathrm{LH}} = \int_{A_p} j_{\phi,\mathrm{LH}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{LH}}$ is the lower-hybrid-driven current,
$j_{\phi,\mathrm{LH}}$ is the toroidal component of the lower-hybrid-driven
current density, and $A_p$ is a poloidal cross-sectional area of the plasma.
The quantity is a whole-plasma net current, so oppositely directed local
contributions may partially cancel. It is a wave-driven contribution within
[current due to wave-driven current
drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) and is distinct from
[current due to electron cyclotron current
drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).

Sign convention: Positive when the lower-hybrid-driven current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Net torque transferred to a plasma particle population through collisional
interactions with other particles, expressed as the corresponding rate of
angular-momentum change.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net angular-momentum transfer to a specified plasma
particle population caused by collisions with other particles. It applies to
electron, fast-particle, and ion populations, including the concrete [ion
collisional torque](name:ion_torque_due_to_collisions) and [fast collisional
torque](name:fast_torque_due_to_collisions) forms.

The scalar torque is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{dL_{\mathrm{pop}}}{dt}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque, $L_{\mathrm{pop}}$
is the relevant angular-momentum component of the population, and $t$ is
time.

The quantity represents the net exchange integrated over the plasma volume
and over the collisional partners included in the population definition. It
is distinct from the local [electron collisional torque
density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), which gives torque
per unit volume.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the nitrogen ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from
the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local nitrogen ion number density at a boundary point is the zeroth
velocity moment summed over ionic charge states:

$$
n_N(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{7} \int f_{N^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_N$ is the nitrogen ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $q$ is the positive
integer ionic charge state, $N^{q+}$ is a nitrogen ion with charge state
$q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $f_{N^{q+}}$ is the phase-space
distribution function for that charge state, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to nitrogen ions and is summed over
charge states from singly ionized nitrogen through fully stripped nitrogen.
It excludes neutral nitrogen and electron density, and it is a local
boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the nitrogen-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary instead averages
the same charge-state-summed nitrogen ion density over the last closed
magnetic flux surface.

items.name: parallel_neutral_velocity
items.description:
Signed component of a neutral species' mean translational flow along the
local magnetic field, density-weighted over contributing internal states.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral velocity is the projection of a selected neutral species'
bulk flow onto the local magnetic-field direction. It describes directed
motion averaged over particle velocities and over the contributing neutral
internal states.

The component is defined by:

$$
u_{0,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf u_0=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_{0,a}\mathbf u_{0,a}}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}n_{0,a}}
$$

where $u_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral velocity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$
is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\mathbf u_0$ is the
[neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) vector. The set $\mathcal A$
contains the included internal states, $a$ labels one such state, $n_{0,a}$
is its neutral number density, and $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is its [bulk neutral
internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), defined
as the mean particle velocity within that state.

Internal-state contributions form a number-density-weighted mean, not a sum
of state velocities. The aggregation applies only to the selected neutral
species and excludes charged particles. This component is distinct from the
flow-speed magnitude, particle flux, and random thermal velocity spread; it
is defined wherever the local magnetic-field direction and neutral mean flow
are defined.

The [poloidal neutral velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_velocity) projects the
same mean neutral flow onto the poloidal direction rather than onto the
magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral mean flow has a component in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity
items.description:
Fickian coefficient relating diffusive electron thermal-energy flux along
magnetic-field lines to the electron thermal-energy-density gradient in that
direction.
items.documentation:
Parallel electron energy diffusivity quantifies gradient-driven transport of
electron thermal energy along the local magnetic field. It is the
field-aligned specialization of [electron energy
diffusivity](name:electron_energy_diffusivity).

The defining energy-density-gradient closure is:

$$
Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,W,\parallel}\,\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\nabla\mathcal{W}_e
$$

where $Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive electron
thermal-energy flux projected along the magnetic field, $D_{e,W,\parallel}$
is this diffusivity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector co-directed with
the local magnetic field, $\mathcal{W}_e$ is the local electron
thermal-energy density, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The minus
sign expresses transport down the field-parallel energy-density gradient.

This local coefficient applies to the electron thermal-energy population,
not to the combined electron and ion energy content. It describes only the
diffusive contribution, excluding convective, advective, and perpendicular
transport. For the down-gradient closure, the coefficient is nonnegative.

The [electron energy diffusion
coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead multiplies
a temperature gradient in a density-normalized heat-flux closure. The two
coefficients are not interchangeable without specifying electron density,
heat capacity, and the treatment of density gradients.

Unlike [poloidal electron energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity), this coefficient
follows the magnetic-field direction, which generally includes both poloidal
and toroidal directions.

items.name: tilt_angle_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Signed inclination of the second side of a parallelogram-shaped oblique
cross-section of a ferritic element, measured counterclockwise from
vertically upward +Z toward decreasing R in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Signed inclination of the second side of a parallelogram-shaped oblique
cross-section of a ferritic element is the $\beta$ orientation angle of that
side in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. It is measured from the vertically upward $+Z$ direction.

Let $\mathbf{t}_\beta$ be the directed vector along the second side, with
radial component $\Delta R_\beta$ along $\hat{R}$ and vertical component
$\Delta Z_\beta$ along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame. The angle is defined by:

$$
\beta = \operatorname{atan2}(-\Delta R_\beta, \Delta Z_\beta)
$$

where $\operatorname{atan2}$ selects the signed quadrant of the directed
side vector.

This quantity specifies orientation only. The first-side $\alpha$
inclination is the inclination angle of a ferritic element, the length of
the $\alpha$ side is the [major length of a ferritic
element](name:major_length_of_ferritic_element), and the length of the
$\beta$ side is the minor length of a ferritic element. When the first-side
and second-side inclinations are both zero, the parallelogram-shaped oblique
cross-section reduces to the rectangular limiting geometry.

Sign convention: Positive when the directed second-side vector is rotated
counterclockwise from the $+Z$ direction toward decreasing $R$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description:
Forward power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the incident RF power traveling
from the transmission line toward the antenna input reference plane.
items.documentation:
Forward power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative RF power
propagating toward the antenna input reference plane from the transmission
line. It is one per-antenna component of the wave-power budget represented
by power of a lower-hybrid antenna.

The per-antenna power components satisfy:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident power arriving at the reference
plane, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the power returning toward the transmission
line, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net power entering the vacuum vessel.
Thus, forward power includes the portion subsequently reflected and is
distinct from [reflected power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and [launched power
of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). The
quantity applies to one antenna and is not an aggregate over multiple
antennas.

items.name: launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the net RF power coupled into
the vacuum vessel toward the plasma, equal to the forward power minus the
reflected power at the launching unit. The launching unit may be an antenna
module, a single antenna, or the complete antenna set, for which the value
is the sum over the constituent units.
items.documentation:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative net RF power
coupled from the launching structure into the vacuum vessel toward the
plasma. It is the net-transfer component of the wave-power budget
represented by [power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The launched power is defined by the balance:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the [forward power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) arriving at the antenna
input reference plane from the transmission line, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is
the [reflected power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) returning toward the
transmission line, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net power entering the
vacuum vessel.

The launching unit may be an antenna module, a single antenna, or the
complete lower-hybrid antenna set. The quantity is extensive, so the
launched power of a composite unit is the sum of the launched powers of its
constituent units.

Launched power excludes the reflected contribution and is distinct from
forward power, which includes the portion subsequently reflected. It denotes
the net power delivered across the launching aperture into the vessel, not
the generator output on the transmission-line side of the reference plane,
and it does not by itself resolve where the power is subsequently deposited
within the plasma.

The [toroidal-mode-resolved launched
power](name:launched_power_per_toroidal_mode_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and
the [jointly toroidal- and poloidal-mode-resolved launched
power](name:launched_power_per_toroidal_and_poloidal_mode_number_of_lower_hybrid_antenna)
are distributions of this same quantity over refractive-index intervals;
integrating them over those intervals recovers the launched power of the
corresponding antenna row.

items.name: radial_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Coefficient scaling the free-streaming cap on the flux of cylindrical radial
momentum carried by one neutral species in a specified internal state in
edge-plasma transport.
items.documentation:
This coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on the
gradient-driven flux of radial [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a
specified neutral species in one internal state. It specializes the
[momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
for that population and momentum component in edge-plasma transport
closures.

The limiting flux magnitude is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\max} = f_{s,R}\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the selected neutral species and internal state,
$f_{s,R}$ is this nonnegative limiter coefficient, $\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}$
is the nonnegative free-streaming reference magnitude for the flux of that
state's radial momentum across an oriented surface, and $\Pi_{s,R}^{\max}$
is the corresponding upper bound on the limited flux magnitude.

The radial component is directed along increasing major radius $R$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from
the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. Radial identifies the transported momentum component, not the
direction of transport across the surface, and does not mean
flux-surface-normal.

The coefficient applies separately to the selected neutral species and
internal state; it is neither summed nor averaged over states or species and
excludes ionic populations. The limiter restricts the controlled flux
magnitude without reversing its direction; it is distinct from momentum
diffusivity and does not specify a particular interpolation between
diffusive and free-streaming limits. The [parallel neutral momentum flux
limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
instead limits transport of magnetic-field-parallel neutral momentum.

items.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal component of the helium-4 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the
H-mode pressure pedestal top, resolved along the direction of increasing
toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Toroidal component of the helium-4 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the
H-mode pressure pedestal top, resolved along the direction of increasing
toroidal angle, is the signed bulk-flow component of helium-4 ions along
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
pedestal top is the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pressure pedestal. As a
species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all
helium-4 ionization charge states in the ion population.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal component at the pedestal top is
defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{ped}}^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} =
\frac{\sum_q n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} \left(\mathbf{v}_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}
{\sum_q n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}}
$$

where $q$ labels helium-4 ionization charge states, $n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}$
is the local number density of charge state $q$,
$\mathbf{v}_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}$ is its fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is
the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$; all quantities are
evaluated at the pedestal-top location.

This quantity is local to the pedestal top and is not an average over the
full pedestal or scrape-off layer. It is a species-level helium-4 velocity,
so it differs from charge-state-resolved helium-4 velocities by the
density-weighted charge-state aggregation and from other isotope velocities
only by the selected ion species.

Sign convention: Positive when the helium-4 ion flow is in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: x_coordinate_of_divertor_target
items.description:
Signed Cartesian x-coordinate locating the geometric center of a divertor
target surface in the right-handed (x, y, z) frame, with +x at toroidal
angle φ = 0.
items.documentation:
The x coordinate of a divertor target is the signed Cartesian position of
the geometric center of its target surface. It locates that center in the
right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$, where $\hat{z}$
is vertical and the positive x direction is horizontal at toroidal angle
$\phi=0$.

The coordinate is defined by projection of the center position onto the
Cartesian x unit vector:

$$
x_c = \mathbf{r}_c \cdot \hat{\mathbf{x}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the position vector of the target-surface geometric
center, $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ is the Cartesian x unit vector, and $x_c$ is the
resulting signed coordinate. The corresponding center location is completed
by the [y coordinate of the divertor
target](name:y_coordinate_of_divertor_target) and [z coordinate of the
divertor target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target); this quantity does
not specify the target surface extent.

Sign convention: Positive when the target center lies in the direction of
increasing Cartesian x from the coordinate origin.

items.name: accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of hydrogen atoms introduced by gas
injection during prefill before plasma breakdown; hydrogen contributes one
count per atom.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the cumulative hydrogen atom inventory delivered by gas
injection during the prefill interval ending at plasma breakdown, expressed
using the equivalent-electron convention. It is the hydrogen-specific
contribution to the hydrogen prefill count.

$$
N_{\mathrm{H,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}N_{\mathrm{H}} = N_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{H}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}(t)\,dt
$$

Here $N_{\mathrm{H,eq}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ are dimensionless
equivalent-electron and atom counts, $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ is hydrogen's atomic
number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen injection rate in s$^{-1}$,
and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in
s. Only pre-breakdown gas injection is included; post-breakdown delivery is
represented by [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: electron_energy_flux
items.description:
Electron energy flux is the signed rate of electron kinetic-energy transport
through an oriented surface per unit physical area.
items.documentation:
Electron energy flux represents net kinetic-energy transport by electrons
across an oriented surface. It includes the total electron energy-transport
contribution rather than only its diffusive or convective part.

The defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{e,W} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n} = \frac{d\dot W_e}{dA}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,W}$ is the signed electron energy flux through the surface,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}$ is the electron kinetic-energy flux vector,
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the selected unit surface normal, $\dot W_e$ is the
signed rate of electron kinetic-energy transfer across the surface, and $A$
is its physical area.

The quantity applies to the electron population without selecting a
particular transport mechanism or plasma region. It excludes energy carried
by ions, neutrals, or electromagnetic fields and is distinct from electron
particle-number flux. No radial, poloidal, or magnetic-field-aligned
direction is implicit.

The convective contribution is the electron energy density multiplied by the
normal projection of the [energy convection
velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity); diffusive transport contributes
separately to the total. The [parallel electron energy
flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux) is the specialization obtained by
choosing the surface normal along the magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the net electron kinetic-energy transport is
in the direction of the selected surface normal.

items.name: diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
items.description:
Signed projection of the heat-viscosity electric-current contribution onto
the local diamagnetic direction in a collisional magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Diamagnetic current density due to heat viscosity is the local diamagnetic
component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity
stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection is

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic current density due to heat
viscosity, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the unit vector along the designated
local diamagnetic direction, perpendicular to the magnetic field. The
positive orientation of this direction must be specified by the local
component convention; the heat-viscosity attribution alone does not
determine it.

This is a local, unaveraged contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density), not a surface-integrated current or the
total current density from all mechanisms. Only the heat-viscosity
contribution is included; the definition imposes no restriction to a
particular plasma region.

Unlike [parallel current density due to heat
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), which
projects the same parent vector along the local magnetic field, this
quantity projects onto the local diamagnetic direction. The diamagnetic
qualifier identifies the projection, not a replacement of the heat-viscosity
mechanism by pressure-gradient-driven current.

Sign convention: Positive when the heat-viscosity current has a component
along the designated positive local diamagnetic direction
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia}}$.

items.name: perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift of one ion
charge state onto a specified direction perpendicular to the magnetic field
in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The perpendicular ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma onto a specified direction perpendicular to the
magnetic field. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the
guiding-center motion of individual ions.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\perp} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,\perp}$ is the signed perpendicular diamagnetic-drift
velocity component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure,
$\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the
signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp$ is the specified positive unit vector perpendicular
to the local magnetic field. Directions may be expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical frame $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry
axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow.

Perpendicularity alone does not select a unique direction within the plane
normal to the magnetic field; the orientation of $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp$
must therefore be specified. This quantity is a signed component, not the
drift-speed magnitude, and its direction is not necessarily cylindrical
radial or flux-surface-normal. Because the diamagnetic drift vector is
perpendicular to the magnetic field, the corresponding [parallel ion
charge-state velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
vanishes.

The species-level [perpendicular ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:perpendicular_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of that species, using
the same perpendicular projection direction. It is not the sum of their
velocity components.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified
ion charge state has a component along the specified positive perpendicular
unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\perp$, expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the complex first-order plasma mass density perturbation
eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability
analysis.
items.documentation:
The imaginary part of the complex perturbed plasma mass density
eigenfunction $\tilde{\rho}_m$ arises when the first-order mass density
perturbation is separated into in-phase and quadrature components relative
to a chosen eigenmode phase and normalization. In the standard perturbation
decomposition $\delta\rho(\mathbf{r}, t) =
\mathrm{Re}[\tilde{\rho}_m(\mathbf{r})\, e^{i(n\phi - \omega t)}]$, where
$n$ is the toroidal mode number, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $\omega$
is the complex eigenfrequency, the eigenfunction splits as:

$$
\tilde{\rho}_m = \tilde{\rho}_\mathrm{re} + i\,\tilde{\rho}_\mathrm{im}
$$

where $\tilde{\rho}_\mathrm{re}$ is the [real
part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part) and
$\tilde{\rho}_\mathrm{im}$ is this quantity. Together they encode the local
amplitude $|\tilde{\rho}_m|$ and spatial phase of the mass density
