perturbation over the poloidal cross-section.

The equilibrium mass density about which the perturbation is defined is
$\rho_{m0} = \sum_s m_s n_s$, where $m_s$ and $n_s$ are the mass and number
density of species $s$; ion contributions dominate in fusion plasmas because
electron mass is negligible. These eigenfunctions are produced by linear MHD
eigenvalue solvers that Fourier-decompose perturbations in the toroidal
direction; the imaginary part is meaningful only relative to the phase
convention and normalization of the specific eigenmode calculation. The
companion quantities
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part)
form a self-consistent set of perturbed thermodynamic eigenfunctions for the
same MHD mode.

items.name: net_ion_momentum_source
items.description:
Net ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to all ion charge states, including all contributing
physical processes.
items.documentation:
Net ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional
momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge
states. It retains the direction of the net transfer rather than reducing it
to a magnitude.

The charge-state and process aggregation is

$$
\mathbf{S}_{i} = \sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{i}}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \mathbf{S}_{i,z,p}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i}$ is the total-ion momentum source vector, $z$ indexes
ion charge states in $\mathcal{Z}_{i}$, $p$ indexes contributing physical
processes in $\mathcal{P}$, and $\mathbf{S}_{i,z,p}$ is the corresponding
source for one charge state and process. The [ion momentum
source](name:ion_momentum_source) defines the same directional
momentum-transfer concept at the general species and projection level.

This quantity includes all ion charge states and excludes neutral species.
Its directional projections are components of the same vector, including the
[parallel net ion momentum source](name:parallel_net_ion_momentum_source).

Sign convention: Positive when a projected component points along its
defined positive direction—$+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, or along the defined positive
field-parallel direction.

items.name: particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Particle flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales a
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on particle flux density while
preserving its direction or sign.
items.documentation:
Particle flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales a
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on particle flux density in a
particle-transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while
preserving the direction or sign assigned by the underlying closure.

For a resolved particle-flux component, the limited flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{p,i}=\operatorname{sgn}\!\left(\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|,L_{p,i}\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{p,i}$ is the limited particle flux density, $p$ identifies
the transported particle population, $i$ identifies the resolved flux
component, $\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure flux
density, $\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless
free-streaming bound, and $L_{p,i}$ is the particle flux limiter
coefficient. The functions $\operatorname{sgn}$ and $|\cdot|$ denote the
sign and magnitude of the unconstrained closure flux, respectively.

The coefficient applies to particle transport rather than energy or momentum
transport. Its population scope may be electrons, aggregate ions, aggregate
neutrals, one specified ionization charge state, or one specified neutral
state; an aggregate form and a state-resolved form retain their respective
population definitions and are not summed across unlike populations. The
[electron particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:electron_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [ion
charge-state particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) are
specific instances of this common quantity.

As a particle-specific specialization of the [flux limiter
coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient), this quantity supplies the
multiplier for a particle flux-density bound; the parent also covers limiter
coefficients for other transported quantities, such as momentum flux.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity
items.description:
Mean directed flow along the local magnetic field for ions of a specified
species and ionization charge state, distinct from their random thermal
motion.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion charge-state velocity is the field-aligned projection of
the bulk flow of ions belonging to one specified species and ionization
charge state. It describes mean directed motion at the position under
consideration.

The component is defined by the projected first velocity moment:

$$
u_{\parallel,Z}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf b}(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf u_Z(\mathbf r)=\frac{\int [\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}(\mathbf r)]f_Z(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_Z(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{\parallel,Z}$ is the parallel velocity component, $\mathbf r$ is
position, $Z$ is the selected ionic charge number, $\mathbf u_Z$ is the [ion
charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), $\mathbf v$ is
particle velocity, and $f_Z$ is the velocity distribution of the selected
species and charge state. The integration element $d^3v$ spans velocity
space. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the
local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, whose magnitude is $|\mathbf B|$.

The particle-velocity average is restricted to the selected charge-state
population; no averaging over other charge states is implied. This is a
signed projection of the parent velocity vector, not its magnitude, a
particle flux, or a random thermal velocity spread. Its definition requires
a nonzero magnetic field and nonzero density of the selected population.

The corresponding [parallel ion velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity) is the
density-weighted mean of these components over all ionic charge states of
the same species.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected charge-state bulk flow has a
component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer
items.description:
Total rate of heat generated within one breeder-blanket material layer by
neutron and photon interactions, excluding external and surface heat loads.
items.documentation:
Nuclear heating power of a breeder-blanket layer is the volume-integrated
rate at which neutron and photon interactions convert radiation energy into
heat within that material layer. It is the nuclear component of heating
power of a breeder-blanket layer, rather than the local volumetric quantity
[nuclear power density of a breeder-blanket
layer](name:nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_layer).

The defining relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc,layer}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{layer}}} \dot{q}_{\mathrm{nuc}}\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{nuc,layer}}$ is the layer-integrated nuclear heating
power, $\dot{q}_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the local nuclear energy-deposition rate
per unit volume, and $V_{\mathrm{layer}}$ is the volume of the specified
material layer.

The integral includes energy deposited by neutron interactions and
absorption of primary or secondary photons within the layer. It excludes
plasma-facing radiative heat loads, incident energy that is not deposited,
and energy deposited outside the layer; the result is non-negative.

items.name: deuterated_methane_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous injection rate of deuterated methane (CD4), counted as
equivalent electrons rather than molecules.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which deuterated methane (CD4) is
supplied as an injected gas, with the rate counted in equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{e,\mathrm{CD4}}(t) = N_{e,\mathrm{CD4}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{CD4}}(t) = 10\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{CD4}}(t)
$$

where $S_{e,\mathrm{CD4}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$N_{e,\mathrm{CD4}}=10$ is the number of electrons in one neutral CD4
molecule, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{CD4}}$ is the molecular injection rate. It
counts carbon and deuterium electrons and is not a particle or mass source
rate.

The time integral of this rate gives the accumulated equivalent-electron
count, such as [accumulated deuterated methane count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_deuterated_methane_count_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
items.description:
Vector electric current-density contribution generated by the divergence of
perpendicular viscous stress in a magnetized charged plasma.
items.documentation:
Perpendicular-viscosity current density is the vector electric-current
contribution attributed to perpendicular viscous stress acting on charged
plasma. The word “perpendicular” identifies the viscous-stress mechanism,
not a restriction of the resulting current vector to directions
perpendicular to the magnetic field.

The current-density contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\perp,\nu}=\sum_s q_s n_s\mathbf{u}_{s,\perp,\nu}
$$

where $q_s$ is the signed charge of species $s$ in coulombs, $n_s$ is its
number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{u}_{s,\perp,\nu}$ is the
species-velocity response attributed to the divergence of perpendicular
viscous stress. The vector may be resolved into radial, toroidal, vertical,
poloidal, parallel, or diamagnetic components, including the [parallel
current-density
component](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) and
[diamagnetic current-density
component](name:diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).
It is distinct from the analogous [current density due to parallel
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity).

items.name: absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description:
Absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic wave
power transferred from one coherent beam to the plasma along its trajectory.
items.documentation:
Absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic wave
power transferred from a single coherent beam to plasma particles along the
beam trajectory. It is summed over the contributing plasma species and is
distinct from the residual wave power represented by
power_of_beam_tracing_beam.

Under the single-beam power balance, the absorbed power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs}} = P_0 - P_{\mathrm{res}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is this absorbed power, $P_0$ is the
[initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam),
and $P_{\mathrm{res}}$ is the residual power of the same beam at the
trajectory endpoint. The total includes contributions represented by
species-resolved quantities such as
[electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam)
and
[ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam).
It excludes power remaining in the wave and power assigned at launch but not
transferred along the traced trajectory.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_major_radius
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged nonnegative perpendicular distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis to points on a nested magnetic flux surface, giving the mean
major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Major radius is the nonnegative perpendicular distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis to a geometric point or specified location. For this
flux-surface-averaged quantity, that distance is averaged over each nested
magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The flux-surface average of major radius is defined by

$$
\langle R\rangle_\psi = \frac{\oint_\psi R\,dl/B_p}{\oint_\psi dl/B_p}
$$

where $\langle R\rangle_\psi$ is the averaged major-radius coordinate,
$\psi$ is the magnetic-flux label identifying the surface, $l$ is poloidal
arc length along that surface, and $B_p$ is the magnitude of the poloidal
magnetic field. The contour integral extends around the complete poloidal
intersection of the nested magnetic flux surface.

This quantity applies to a complete magnetic flux surface and aggregates the
local [major radius](name:major_radius) using the flux-surface weighting
defined by the inverse poloidal-field magnitude. It is therefore distinct
from pointwise major radius and contains no point-specific or localized
evaluation.

The quantity is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [major
radius](name:major_radius). It must not be confused with
[flux-surface-averaged inverse of major
radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius), which averages
the reciprocal $1/R$ rather than averaging $R$ itself; consequently, it is
not generally the reciprocal of that neighboring average.

items.name: fast_ion_critical_energy
items.description:
Threshold energy at which Coulomb drag on a fast ion from thermal electrons
equals that from thermal ions, determining the partition of fast-ion power
between electron and ion heating channels.
items.documentation:
The fast-ion critical energy $E_c$ separates two collisional energy-loss
regimes for suprathermal ions decelerating in a thermal plasma. Above $E_c$,
fast ions lose energy predominantly to thermal electrons via Coulomb drag;
below $E_c$, energy is deposited preferentially in the bulk thermal ion
population, directly controlling the electron-to-ion power balance in
transport modeling.

The critical energy follows from equating the electron and ion frictional
forces on the decelerating fast ion:

$$
E_c = T_e \left(\frac{3\sqrt{\pi}}{4}\right)^{2/3} \left(\frac{m_f}{m_e}\right)^{1/3} \left(\sum_i \frac{n_i Z_i^2}{n_e} \frac{m_f}{m_i}\right)^{2/3}
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature, $m_f$ and $m_e$ are the fast-ion
and electron masses, $n_i$, $Z_i$, and $m_i$ are the density, charge number,
and mass of background ion species $i$, and $n_e$ is the electron density.

The critical energy varies radially through its dependence on local $T_e$
and plasma composition and is computed from kinetic plasma data rather than
measured directly. For NBI-injected deuterons at $T_e \approx 3$–$8$ keV,
$E_c$ falls in the range 30–150 keV; for fusion alpha particles, it reaches
several hundred keV at reactor-relevant temperatures.

This quantity is the ion-specific form of fast_particle_critical_energy,
which spans both electron and ion fast-particle populations. The equivalent
name with the thermalization mechanism made explicit is
critical_fast_particle_energy_due_to_thermalization. The thermal-plasma
heating power that accumulates as fast ions slow through $E_c$ is quantified
by
[thermal_particle_heating_power_due_to_thermalization_of_fast_particles](name:thermal_particle_power_due_to_thermalization).
